stories.Headline: Anthropic completes largest IPO in history with 1.5 trillion dollar valuation
stories.Summary:
Anthropic completed the biggest initial public offering in history on November 19, 2026. The San Francisco company became the first major artificial intelligence lab to list publicly. This record breaking debut occurred despite recent jitters among some investors regarding the AI sector. The company raised a total of US$81 billion through the offering of its shares. This event marks a superlative debut for the maker of the Claude AI system.

The company offered 980 million shares at a price of US$83 each before trading began. Shares opened at US$111.50 and closed at US$97.17, creating a first day value of US$1.75 trillion. At noon Eastern time, the valuation spiked to US$2.01 trillion, which is 1am Singapore time on November 20. This exceeds the US$75 billion raised by SpaceX in June and US$26.5 billion by SK Hynix in July. Saudi Aramco previously raised US$25.6 billion in 2019, while SpaceX ended its first day at US$2.1 trillion.

CEO Amodei is the person responsible for taking the safety approach of the company public. He decided to proceed with the listing despite growing unease among the public about technology risks. The company leadership pushed forward even with fears that artificial intelligence might be running amok. They aimed to establish the lab as a publicly traded entity during the current AI boom. This move allows the company to join a small group of tech giants with 13 digit wealth.

Investors expressed worry about market volatility and the possibility of a wider artificial intelligence bubble. The general public remains uneasy about the overall risks associated with this powerful new technology. Eleven companies in the S&P 500 have reached the trillion dollar club, including Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia. Apple leads this group at US$5.1 trillion, followed by Microsoft at US$3.8 trillion and Nvidia at US$3.6 trillion. SpaceX and Anthropic have also joined this club, although they are not yet in the S&P 500.

Apple was the first corporation to pass the trillion dollar threshold back in the year 2018. A trillion US dollar bills laid end to end would stretch 156 million kilometres, surpassing the distance to the sun. One trillion is a thousand times greater than one billion and a million times more than one million. The US Census Bureau states there are more than 8.2 billion people currently living on Earth. Dividing one trillion dollars among everyone would give each person almost US$122.

The market cap of SpaceX has fallen to closer to US$1.95 trillion since its own record debut. Anthropic finished its first day of trading over 17 percent higher than its initial public offering price. The company now stands as the second business to debut with a value over one trillion dollars. Future performance on the public market remains uncertain as the company navigates these high valuations. The articles leave open how the company will fare as investors monitor the stability of the AI boom.

stories.Headline: Harvard researchers estimate US data centers emit as much greenhouse gas as Denmark
stories.Summary:
Harvard University researchers published a study on Monday regarding pollution from the largest data centers in the United States. The report found that 400 of these facilities produced more heat trapping gas in one year than Denmark. Meanwhile, negotiators at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, launched a voluntary pledge for clean energy on Monday. This initiative seeks to make companies and countries more open about their emissions and their water and power consumption. The pledge also encourages using the power of artificial intelligence to help solve the difficult problem of climate change.

The Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge was launched by the International Telecommunication Union and the host country of Turkey. It requires that data centers use clean power, efficient energy systems, and responsible hardware recycling to reduce electronic waste. Harvard researchers analyzed 403 large centers from May 2024 to April 2025, estimating 28.3 million tons of carbon dioxide. These centers used 82 terawatt hours of electricity, with over half coming from fossil fuels, powering nearly 7 million homes. The pledge received 90 endorsements, including Germany, Brazil, and South Korea, but only Alibaba among major tech companies signed.

United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell said that future emissions savings cannot excuse the rising pollution happening right now. He stated that people should not accept higher bills and deeper inequality in exchange for promises of a better tomorrow. COP31 President Murat Kurum said world leaders must openly discuss the growing energy consumption of AI and set terms. ITU Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin said international cooperation is necessary to make AI sustainable for countries vulnerable to climate impacts. These leaders believe that the environmental footprint of AI must be managed responsibly as the technology is deployed.

Former Vice President Al Gore said he is less concerned about AI emissions and hopes computing power fights climate change. Caleb Max of the National Artificial Intelligence Association said fears about water and energy consumption may be overblown. Philip Newell of Climate Action Against Disinformation said companies are selling hope while they are hiding the harms. Major tech firms like Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon were not among the publicly identified signatories of the pledge. These companies are affected by a 240 percent rise in electricity consumption between 2022 and 2025.

The study found that emissions are two to three times higher than previous research showed, resembling the state of Michigan. Harvard professor Francesca Dominici noted that plans for 2,000 more data centers make the current pollution levels more worrisome. The International Energy Agency estimated that global data centers consumed 485 terawatt hours of electricity in 2025. AI focused facilities saw consumption rise by 50 percent, which is faster than the overall global electricity demand. This growth has prompted a push for new power generation that prevents big tech companies from reaching goals.

The International Energy Agency projects that worldwide data center electricity consumption could reach 950 terawatt hours by 2030. Some companies like BaRupOn are building campuses in Texas and North Dakota to capture waste heat for electricity. The IEA estimates that captured heat could provide warmth for 10 percent of European homes by 2030. The articles leave open whether voluntary commitments can influence an industry that is investing heavily in computing infrastructure. It remains unclear if the pledge will secure more endorsements from major technology groups before talks end Friday.

stories.Headline: Wenge AI adds Google and Apple sign-in options for international ScienceOra users
stories.Summary:
Wenge AI announced a new update for its ScienceOra platform on November 20, 2026. The company added Google and Apple sign-in options for users of its international site. This change happened in Shenzhen, China, to help researchers access the platform. The update streamlines the registration and sign-in process for overseas scientific researchers. It provides a faster and more convenient way to enter the AI for Science platform.

Users can now authenticate using existing Google or Apple accounts instead of lengthy forms. Apple sign-in is currently available on the web version of the ScienceOra platform. The system identifies whether to create new accounts or sign in based on email status. It improves how third-party accounts link and provides clearer prompts for the Hide My Email feature. These changes aim to reduce duplicate registrations and resolve common sign-in friction for users.

Wenge AI is an enterprise AI company that develops proprietary foundation models and platforms. The company was founded by a team of AI scientists from the Chinese Academy of Sciences. They stated that the refinements maintain a consistent account experience for their international users. The firm intends to continue refining the product experience based on the needs of researchers. They aim to make scientific exploration and access to research tools more seamless.

Overseas researchers are affected by these changes to the AI-powered scientific research and decision-support platform. ScienceOra uses the ScienceOne Scientific Foundation Model to bring together data, tools, and specialized research agents. Meanwhile, the Korean Fair Trade Commission is requiring overseas platforms to appoint legal representatives by January 21. This rule affects companies like Apple, Google, Alibaba, and OpenAI to resolve consumer disputes. The FTC official said that failing to comply will lead to immediate investigations.

The FTC rule applies to businesses with global annual sales of at least 1 trillion won. It also covers platforms with at least 1 million average monthly Korean users during a specific period. Another criterion includes businesses that caused significant consumer harm after violating local e-commerce laws. The FTC met with Alibaba, Temu, and OpenAI on October 28 to review industry feedback. These guidelines clarify the obligations for overseas businesses under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.

The FTC will operate a three-month grace period after the system takes effect in January. This period helps companies adjust but does not delay the January 21 appointment deadline. The domestic representative will serve as a formal communication channel for legal notices and investigations. The regulator plans to monitor the implementation of this system and consider further improvements. The articles leave open how many companies will successfully appoint representatives before the deadline.

stories.Headline: Margin debt hits record high as Wall Street faces bubble risk
stories.Summary:
On November 21, 2026, Sean Williams wrote in The Motley Fool that Wall Street may be watching a $1.5 trillion bubble burst in real time. He said the bubble is not artificial intelligence but outstanding margin debt, the money investors borrow from brokers to buy or short securities. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite had powered higher since the 2022 bear market bottomed. The Dow rose up to 90% from its trough, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq more than doubled. On the same day the S&P 500 stood at 6,910.39, down 3.7%, the Dow at 48,147.33, down 1.9%, and the Nasdaq at 22,617.73, down 5.3%.

Outstanding margin debt rose 77% over 14 months to an all-time high of $1.502 trillion in June 2026, up from April 2025. Over the previous four months it fell from $1.502 trillion to $1.448 trillion as of October. Since 1998 margin debt rose at least 65% over a short period on four occasions, and the previous three were followed by declines. From March 1999 to March 2000 margin debt surged 80% to almost $300 billion, and by October 2002 the S&P 500 and Nasdaq had shed 49% and 78%. From June 2006 to July 2007 margin debt jumped 66% over 13 months to about $416 billion before the Great Recession lopped 57% off the S&P 500. From March 2020 to October 2021 margin debt catapulted 95% to a then-peak of $936 billion in 19 months, and the 2022 bear market wiped away one-fifth, one-quarter and one-third of the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq.

Williams credited historically low peak marginal corporate income tax rates with fueling record share buyback activity by S&P 500 companies. He also cited stock-split euphoria and record-breaking initial public offerings as intriguing retail investors. He said the AI infrastructure build-out was the primary catalyst behind Wall Street's gains but not the only reason stocks were higher. He wrote that history has a way of rhyming on Wall Street and that historical precedent often sets the tone. He said margin acts as leverage, amplifying gains when a security moves in the desired direction and magnifying losses when it moves the opposite way, on top of owing the broker interest.

Williams said that when investors lighten up their leverage following a parabolic increase, it has historically been the ultimate red flag that a bubble is about to burst. He said there is no single predictive tool that can tell investors precisely when a downturn will begin, how long it will last or how steep it will be. He said history conclusively shows downturns have always represented buying opportunities for optimistic, long-term-minded investors. He said that if the margin debt bubble does burst, opportunity will await. He noted Stock Advisor's total average return of 768% compared with 199% for the S&P 500, as of November 21, 2026.

Williams cited Bespoke Investment Group, which six months ago calculated the calendar-day length of every S&P 500 bull and bear market since September 1929. Bespoke found the typical bear market lasted just 286 calendar days over the last 97 years, while the average bull market persisted about 3.6 times as long, or 1,023 calendar days. Bespoke said no bear market took longer than 630 calendar days to find its trough. Bespoke said just over half, 14 of 27, of S&P 500 bull markets since September 1929 lasted longer than 630 calendar days. Bespoke said the bull market that began on 10/12/22 was the 9th longest in S&P 500 history, surpassing the 1,324-day bull that ended on 2/9/1966.

In a Fortune commentary on November 18, 2026, Mark Minevich wrote that the AI gold rush as we knew it is over and that unlimited spending and unquestioned valuations are finished. He said global AI funding was $239.1 billion in Q1 of 2026, $153.1 billion in Q2 and $103.3 billion in Q3. He said Nvidia lost nearly $2 trillion in market value since its October 6 record, over 30% of what was the most valuable company on earth, gone in under six weeks. He said Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12 after 33 years, the CFO is interim CEO and Congress has called Huang to testify. He said the company at the center of the AI economy now carries succession risk and national security exposure at the same time.

stories.Headline: California Attorney General subpoenas Nvidia over potential AI chip leaks and CEO misconduct
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the top executive of Nvidia last week after admitting to a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. The sixty three year old co-founded the Santa Clara company in 1993 but stepped down following the revelation of his affair. He also allegedly had a second affair with the vice president of healthcare and a third with another subordinate employee. California Attorney General Rob Bonta served the multitrillion dollar company with an investigative subpoena on Thursday, November 19, 2026. This legal action seeks to determine if the company misled the public and investors regarding the handling of this scandal.

The subpoena asks if confidential information or advanced artificial intelligence chips were sent to China, which would violate national security interests. Bonta is evaluating if Nvidia violated California law, similar to a lawsuit his office filed against OpenAI over misleading claims. The board appointed Colette Kress, the chief financial officer and executive vice president since 2013, to serve as interim CEO. On Tuesday, the company reported third quarter revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, which is an increase of 103 percent. Nvidia also stopped reporting its Singapore revenue separately just as scrutiny of the Singaporean company Megaspeed began to arise.

Attorney General Rob Bonta stated that companies cannot mislead their investors and that the conduct of Huang and Nvidia raises red flags. Nvidia launched an internal investigation and claimed there is no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised. Chairman Harvey C. Jones said the board unanimously accepted the resignation and acted in the best interest of all stakeholders. Jensen Huang posted on X that he made serious mistakes in his personal life and did not meet expected standards. He stated he would be honored to return as CEO to help the company navigate complex geopolitical and market dynamics.

Over 180,000 people signed a petition for the return of Huang, an effort supported by Elon Musk and other tech executives. President Donald Trump believes the former CEO had no idea he was targeted by a spy, though the FBI is investigating. House Democrats are investigating if Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick improperly influenced the chip business because his family has holdings in Nvidia. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the Commerce Department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed over possible violations of export rules. The shake up has rattled markets and raised questions about whether the U.S. Commerce Department was complicit or incompetent.

The Commerce Department is conducting a years long investigation into Megaspeed for allegedly skirting export rules governing the powerful AI chips. This investigation included an interview with Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed chief executive and the woman with whom Jensen Huang had an affair. U.S. intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang may be a Chinese spy, and she left her role at Megaspeed in 2025. Megaspeed is conducting its own internal investigation into the matter while the Justice Department pursues criminal conduct. The Commerce Department claims a strong track record of bringing semiconductor smugglers to justice through its own excellent work.

The board confirmed on Tuesday that Jensen Huang would not be reinstated as CEO despite calls from President Trump and his allies. Democrats in Congress will gain greater investigative and subpoena powers in January after winning control of both chambers in midterm elections. The California Department of Justice has not released further information regarding the current status of its investigation into the company. It remains open whether the Commerce Department's failure to blacklist Megaspeed was a result of incompetence or intentional influence. The articles leave unresolved whether any specific confidential data or advanced chips actually reached China through these romantic relationships.

stories.Headline: HHS watchdog warns of cybersecurity and AI governance risks at HHS
stories.Summary:
The HHS Office of Inspector General issued an annual report on Tuesday, November 18, 2026, warning of cybersecurity and AI governance risks at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The report placed cybersecurity, AI and related tech issues among the top five categories of management and performance challenges facing HHS in 2026. The OIG said HHS faces persistent cyber weaknesses, challenges overseeing artificial intelligence, growing third-party security risks and pressure to strengthen HIPAA enforcement. The watchdog warned that cyberattacks and related threats can jeopardize critical HHS operations and programs. The report said these threats could potentially compromise the health and welfare of the individuals HHS serves.

The OIG said HHS's overall enterprise information security program has not yet reached the desired level of effectiveness, and implementation varies across programs. It called on HHS to ensure consistent implementation of strong safeguards across operating divisions. The report warned that rapidly expanding AI adoption, dubbed "super intelligence" by the Trump administration, presents governance and security challenges when risks are not fully understood or tested before deployment. HHS in its 2025 inventory identified 446 AI use cases, including applications supporting core government functions. The OIG said responsible adoption requires clear governance, disciplined implementation and continuous oversight so decisionmakers can weigh benefits and risks.

The OIG cited several audits from the past two years, including a 2025 cyber-related audit of the National Institutes of Health's All of Us research program and a 2024 security review of the HHS office of the secretary's cloud infrastructure unit. It also cited 2026 findings of weaknesses in cybersecurity protections of Medicare enrollee data at a large unnamed hospital in the southeastern U.S. The OIG further cited a 2025 settlement related to false claims allegations involving vulnerabilities in genomic sequencing systems from Illumina Inc. The OIG wrote that effective cybersecurity must extend to the thousands of HHS contractors, grantees and other external entities engaged by HHS programs. It said effective cybersecurity for many HHS programs will depend on these parties implementing solutions that mitigate threats specific to their operations.

Attorney Lee Kim, founder of consulting firm Keytera, said HHS should have a plan for reducing technical debt, including legacy IT and OT systems, and should implement compensating controls if systems cannot be modernized. Kim said HHS should regularly test redundancy, failover, incident response, business continuity and disaster recovery plans, and that regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing are essential. Nitin Natarajan, founder of consulting firm NN Global LLC and former CISA deputy director during the Biden administration, said technical debt at most organizations far exceeds available modernization budgets. Natarajan said this challenge is compounded when AI tools are deployed without a full understanding of their impacts on existing systems. He cited recent router issues allegedly at the center of last week's Federal Aviation Administration outage as underscoring risks involving legacy equipment.

The OIG said healthcare organizations remain attractive targets for cybercriminals because of the sensitive information they maintain and their dependence on interconnected technologies. It said limited financial resources, legacy technology and shortages of cybersecurity professionals further complicate efforts to defend against attacks that can compromise patient information and disrupt essential healthcare services. The OIG urged HHS to adapt its oversight and enforcement of HIPAA to better address evolving privacy and cybersecurity threats. It said HHS must work within existing HIPAA authorities to ensure oversight and enforcement keep pace with evolving risks to protected health information. The report said the findings underscore challenges facing HHS as it works to improve its own cybersecurity practices while overseeing security and privacy protections across the nation's healthcare sector.

Kim said HHS should establish technical standards for developing, evaluating and deploying AI systems, including standards for training and testing data and processes, model architecture, and model modifications and updates. Kim said models should be tested for accuracy, bias, uncertainty, data leakage, adversarial vulnerabilities and other unintended behavior. Natarajan said he encourages healthcare sector organizations to "deploy AI with intent" and to fully understand the tools they implement, including cybersecurity, transparency, information security and privacy matters. Natarajan said AI vendors need to be transparent about their tools and the impacts those tools may have on connected data or systems. HHS did not immediately respond to ISMG's request for comment on the OIG's findings and how the department is addressing the watchdog agency's concerns.

stories.Headline: Google picks Blue Origin to launch TPU-equipped Project Suncatcher satellites in early 2029
stories.Summary:
Google has selected Blue Origin for the first heavy-lift launch of Project Suncatcher, and the New Glenn rocket is scheduled to place satellites equipped with TPUs into a sun-synchronous orbit in early 2029. Each of those satellites will carry computing power comparable to a data center rack, according to the company. The two companies have signed an agreement for launch services, and this will be the first launch dedicated entirely to Project Suncatcher. Through this project, Google is investigating whether a network of solar-powered satellites, equipped with its own Tensor Processing Units, can scale up machine learning compute in space.

According to Google, the launch builds on its collaboration with other satellite and launch partners, and the company says solar panels in Earth orbit can generate up to eight times as much energy as comparable panels on Earth. Google also says the approach would reduce demand for computing power on terrestrial power grids. The first step was more modest, because Google worked with Planet on a prototype satellite that was launched on a SpaceX mission to determine whether TPUs could survive launch, radiation, vacuum, and extreme temperatures. That test was explicitly a hardware experiment and not a functioning data center in space, and Google plans to test laser links between satellites using two satellites in 2027. The 2029 launch is on a different scale, with the satellites interconnected via optical links to create a distributed data center.

Travis Beals, Senior Director of Project Suncatcher at Google, calls the agreement a crucial milestone on the roadmap and describes Project Suncatcher as a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit. Jordan Charles, Senior Vice President of New Glenn at Blue Origin, says the rocket's heavy-lift capacity and large payload volume give customers the flexibility to bring new capabilities to orbit. Google wants to take advantage of sunlight, which is available almost continuously in orbit, and the company frames the effort as a way to scale machine learning compute in space. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the planned 2027 laser link test and the early 2029 launch.

stories.Headline: Professor Sarfo warns students that over-reliance on AI blunts critical thinking
stories.Summary:
Professor Frederick K. Sarfo, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development, cautioned students against over-relying on Artificial Intelligence, according to a Ghanaian Times report published on November 20, 2026. He warned that unchecked dependence on digital tools risks blunting students' critical thinking skills and their memory retention. The report said he made the remarks in Kumasi, in a story filed by Kingsley E. Hope. The caution was carried in the Ghanaian Times, which also invited readers to follow its WhatsApp channel.

Professor Sarfo said it is a universal fact that AI is fundamentally changing the way students learn and conduct research, and that AI is useful to students for several reasons. He said research evidence shows that heavy reliance on AI reduces brain activity, critical thinking skills, and students' ability to recall events, facts, or information. He advised students to use AI or technology wisely and appropriately in their academic activities. Otherwise, he cautioned, they will become passive learners instead of active learners.

Separately, a University of the West Indies professor warned that excessive dependence on Artificial Intelligence could weaken students' ability to think critically, ABS TV Radio Antigua & Barbuda reported on November 19, 2026. The warning came during a Vice Chancellor's Forum on Tuesday marking the 30th anniversary of the School of Graduate Studies and Research. Dr Dwyane Devonish, Director of Graduate Studies at the UWI Cave Hill campus, said navigating the technology is critical. He provided the caution while making it clear that AI presents significant opportunities.

Both reports place the warnings in the same week of November 2026, one from a Ghanaian university leader and one from a Caribbean graduate studies director. The Ghanaian Times report was published on November 20, 2026, and the ABS TV Radio report on November 19, 2026. Neither article says what policies, if any, the two institutions will adopt in response to the warnings. Neither article states what happens next beyond the advice given to students.

stories.Headline: Disseqt AI raises $8 million to expand AI governance platform and hire in India
stories.Summary:
Disseqt AI, an AI governance and assurance startup, raised $8 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, TechGig reported on November 20, 2026. The round also drew participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland, according to the company's press release. Angel investors included senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, the release stated. Former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid invested in his individual capacity, Disseqt said. Inc42 reported the same $8 million round on November 19, 2026, describing the company as one that builds AI agents for AI governance and testing.

The fresh funds will be used to expand the company's global enterprise customer base, according to TechGig. Disseqt also plans hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, the report said. Inc42 reported that the capital will scale operations across the UK and international markets. The $8 million figure is about ₹75 crore, Inc42 stated. While headquartered in Ireland, Disseqt's engineering and AI teams are based in Bengaluru, and it has customer-facing operations across the UK, Ireland and India, according to its website.

Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy founded Disseqt AI in late 2025, the articles state. Kumar, the CEO and cofounder, said every enterprise is handing real work to AI agents but very few can prove those agents are safe, fair and within policy. He said this gap often stops ambitious AI projects from going live and is what Disseqt was built to close. He said the funding lets the company bring that standard to more enterprises around the world. Atri, the COO, is India-based, and both Kumar and Atri are graduates of IIIT Allahabad, Inc42 reported.

Disseqt provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents, according to TechGig. The platform assesses AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforces company policies once they go live and continuously monitors their behaviour. It can block outputs that violate organisational policies and maintains audit trails for compliance and oversight. Enterprises can test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information and check for other vulnerabilities before deployment. Inc42 reported that the platform lets compliance, security and IT teams test agentic workflows for vulnerabilities and data-leak risks prior to deployment, enforce real-time policy guardrails in production, block non-compliant outputs and maintain audit trails independent of underlying model providers.

Disseqt said it has deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases, TechGig reported. In a project for a global sports league's fan engagement agent serving 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80 per cent to 99 per cent across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. No unsafe outputs were detected after fixes were implemented, according to the report. The company also provides assurance services for a credit card services programme at a large European bank. Disseqt has partnered with Indian IT companies Infosys, Cognizant, HCLTech, Mphasis and Tata Technologies as Global System Integrators to deploy its platforms for their enterprise clients, Inc42 reported.

The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance, TechGig stated. McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey found 40 per cent of companies with over $1 billion in annual revenues were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27 per cent a year earlier. Inc42's Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026 found AI startup funding more than tripled year on year to $438 million in the September quarter. Overall funding raised by Indian startups increased by just 5 per cent year on year, Inc42 reported. The investment marks another bet on the emerging AI governance and assurance segment, according to TechGig.

Why So Blu published its own article about the same release on November 19th, 2026, written by Jordan Grout. The sci-fi drama stars Haley Joel Osment, Jude Law, Frances O'Connor, Brendan Gleeson, and William Hurt. The film is rated PG-13 and is distributed by Paramount Pictures and Alliance Home Entertainment.

The release arrives on Limited Edition 4K UHD Steelbook on December 15th, and readers are invited to pre-order their copy through a link in the Why So Blu article. stories.Headline: AI tools help businesses and creators produce images and videos faster while requiring human review
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is driving the evolution of digital media through automated creative production and personalized online experiences. Businesses, designers, and content creators are adopting these intelligent technologies to improve efficiency and deliver engaging content. These systems allow users to transform written descriptions into illustrations, realistic photographs, and artistic compositions. AI video generators enable the development of animated scenes and promotional clips using text and images. This technological shift is occurring as digital competition increases and high quality visual materials become a priority.

The process requires machine learning systems trained on large data collections to identify patterns between visual elements and movement. Seedance 2.5 Flash is a technology that demonstrates how written concepts can be transformed into moving visual sequences. Dreamina is another platform that offers users an environment to explore AI supported visual production for digital content. These tools are used for website graphics, advertising campaigns, product presentations, and educational illustrations in various industries. The technology is applied in e-commerce for product catalogs and in education to make learning materials more interactive.

The Daily Iowan reports that AI helps organizations overcome traditional production challenges while opening new possibilities for innovation. They state that AI serves as a creative resource for professionals and an accessible starting point for beginners. Technology Org explains that generative video systems create new visual material rather than just arranging existing footage. They note that maintaining temporal consistency between frames is one of the major technical challenges in generative development. These sources suggest that combining AI capabilities with professional judgment helps organizations achieve better quality standards.

Online retailers are affected because they can simplify the development of digital product content and personalized marketing materials. Teachers and trainers can use these technologies to develop supporting materials and visual explanations more efficiently. Students benefit from visual explanations that make difficult subjects easier to understand through automatically generated videos. Independent creators use these tools to experiment with fictional environments, promotional concepts, and digital storytelling. Professional designers are affected as they integrate generated sequences into workflows involving editing software and sound production tools.

Traditional digital artwork required a combination of technical knowledge, design experience, and specialized software for every design element. Traditional video production relied exclusively on cameras, recording equipment, and conventional editing techniques to create moving images. Generative video differs because it must interpret subjects, surroundings, and lighting before producing a coherent visual sequence. This process involves managing spatial information for individual frames and temporal information for movement and continuity. High computational processing is required to coordinate multiple frames based on the requested duration, resolution, and complexity.

The next stage of development will likely involve greater connections between image generation, video creation, animation, and interactive media. Future improvements in machine learning and visual understanding could make creative systems more accurate and responsive to instructions. Users must still review generated content to ensure accuracy, originality, and suitability for the intended purpose. Businesses must continue to consider copyright requirements, privacy concerns, and transparency when using these AI generated materials. The articles leave open how researchers will fully resolve visual distortions and improve motion representation in videos.

stories.Headline: California regulators bar Waymo robotaxis from freeways and Waymo pauses US freeway rides
stories.Summary:
Waymo suspended driverless freeway rides across the United States after the California Department of Motor Vehicles barred its robotaxis from the state’s freeways, an order issued on November 11, 2026, and made public on November 17. The California restrictions followed two incidents in early November, when three Waymo vehicles entered a closed construction area on US Highway 101 near Burlingame on November 5 and another vehicle on Interstate 280 reportedly failed to respond appropriately to California Highway Patrol officers conducting a traffic break on November 6. Regulators concluded that recurring problems with construction zones and emergency vehicles created an immediate public safety concern, despite corrective measures taken after similar incidents earlier in the year. Waymo said the construction zone incidents caused no injuries or collisions, and the company has not announced a date for restoring freeway rides.

Although the order applies only to California, Waymo voluntarily paused freeway operations in all its other US markets while it reviews its autonomous driving systems, and driverless rides remain available on ordinary urban streets. The company runs commercial driverless service in 15 American cities, including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin, and the suspension removes freeway connections such as those between San Francisco and Silicon Valley. Longer trips that once used freeways may now follow slower urban roads, which could increase travel times, particularly for airport journeys during heavy traffic. Waymo advises passengers to check estimated journey times in its app and allow enough time for security and check-in, and travelers should not assume every airport or destination is served, because pickup areas and operating boundaries differ between cities.

Waymo said it is working with the California DMV and other state authorities to address the concerns and will resume freeway operations once the necessary safety improvements have been demonstrated. The California restrictions will stay in place until Waymo shows sufficient improvements to its autonomous driving technology and can respond safely to construction zones, emergency vehicles and changing freeway conditions. The company previously suspended freeway operations in May 2026 over safety concerns involving construction zones, then introduced software improvements and began restoring freeway access in July. The latest restrictions are another setback for the company’s efforts to expand autonomous transportation across major US cities, and freeway travel remains unavailable until further notice.

stories.Headline: RadixArk releases DaisyRose-27B coding model trained exclusively with reinforcement learning
stories.Summary:
RadixArk released its first open-weight agentic coding model, DaisyRose-27B, during the week of November 20, 2026. This thinking model was post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B using only reinforcement learning without any distillation or supervised fine-tuning. The development process involved 18 days of training on 144 H200 GPUs, totaling 63,000 GPU-hours. This effort utilized the open-source RL framework called Miles and a specialized sandbox environment known as AgentENV.

The model features 27.8 billion dense parameters and a context window of 262,144 tokens. It requires a single GPU to run, with memory needs ranging from 23 GB for NVFP4 on Blackwell GPUs to 52 GB for BF16. The architecture maintains the Qwen3.8-27B design, including 64 decoder layers and a 27-layer vision encoder for processing images. Performance improved across seven benchmarks, most notably on Terminal Bench 4.1, where the pass@1 score rose from 5.6 to 12.0.

RadixArk developed the model using 1,200 curated tasks created with Eigent AI to address specific failures of the base model. The company stated that their internal backend achieved a 37 percent model flop utilization, which provided a two-fold speedup in throughput. They reported that their sandbox costs were approximately 80 percent lower than those of popular cloud providers. While the model leads in IFBench with a score of 82.4, the developers admitted it still trails larger mixture-of-experts models on difficult agentic tasks.

stories.Headline: Google gives IIT Kharagpur $5 million to fund AI research and education
stories.Summary:
Google announced on November 21, 2026, that it would give IIT Kharagpur $5 million, or Rs 46 crore, for advanced AI research, education and technology development. Google made the announcement through its official blog. Google CEO Sundar Pichai, an IIT Kharagpur alumnus, announced the initiative as part of the company's efforts to support AI research and develop scientific and technical talent in India. The funding will help the institute's researchers and students work on AI-based solutions. The grant covers AI applications in Indian languages, agriculture, materials science and educational technology, and AI training for students, faculty members and teachers.

The funding focuses on three main areas: advanced AI research, educational opportunities and AI capacity building across the institute. Under the research component, projects will use AI to address real-world challenges in Indic languages, materials science, agriculture and educational technology. The focus on Indic languages aims to support AI solutions that work across India's diverse language landscape. The second part will expand AI learning through training programmes and curriculum for students, faculty members and teachers. The third area will strengthen IIT Kharagpur's AI capabilities through AI frameworks and tools for its technological ecosystem and campus research.

Pichai said IIT Kharagpur is doing important work in areas such as Indic languages, agriculture and education. He said the collaboration would help accelerate this work and create opportunities for the next generation of students. Pichai also said India is increasingly at the forefront of innovation. He said initiatives like this can help make the benefits of AI accessible to people across the country. The aim is to help more people gain AI knowledge and skills and prepare the next generation of scientific and technical talent.

A meta-analysis involving 14,321 participants found positive learning outcomes for intelligent tutoring systems compared with conventional large-group instruction (Ma et al., 2014). A randomized study of 194 university physics students found a carefully designed AI tutor produced greater short-term learning gains in less time than comparison classroom-based active-learning instruction (Kestin et al., 2025). In a randomized experiment with nearly 1,000 high school mathematics students, those using unrestricted GPT-4 performed 48 percent better during practice but scored 17 percent lower on later independent examinations without AI than the control group (Bastani et al., 2025). Stanford University's November 2026 SCALE review synthesized 52 causal studies and found promising outcomes from interactive tutoring, adaptive instruction, sequenced practice and feedback, while warning that using AI to complete academic work can undermine independent performance (Walker et al., 2026). In Stanford's Tutor CoPilot experiment, more than 700 tutors and over 1,000 students took part, and students whose tutors received AI assistance were 4 percentage points more likely to master mathematics topics, with gains of 9 percentage points among students working with lower-rated tutors (Wang et al., 2025).

The articles say education is not measured by how quickly learners finish assignments but by how deeply they understand and independently apply knowledge. They say AI's educational value depends less on technological sophistication than on how teachers and students use it. They say apparent academic improvement may sometimes reflect dependence rather than competence. They say favorable student attitudes toward AI did not consistently translate into measurable learning gains. They say teachers contribute judgment, empathy, motivation, contextual understanding and relationships, and that AI can supplement these strengths.

The articles say children are still developing literacy, numeracy, critical thinking, self-regulation and social intelligence, and that unrestricted AI assistance may be particularly risky when learners lack foundational knowledge to evaluate machine-generated responses. They say in basic education AI should function primarily as a guided tutor offering differentiated explanations, additional exercises, mastery-based practice, formative feedback and language support. They say universities can use AI for research exploration, simulations, programming, writing feedback, professional case analysis and complex problem-solving. They say these applications require safeguards for academic integrity, source verification, independent scholarship and disciplinary expertise. They say AI can fabricate references and deliver inaccurate explanations with unwarranted confidence, so students must learn to question, verify and responsibly apply its output.

stories.Headline: Tech Talent Project urges incoming leaders to prioritize in-house technology hiring as AI reshapes public services
stories.Summary:
Following the 2026 midterms, a new class of elected officials is preparing to take office, and government technology experts say building stronger in-house technology teams should be among their top priorities. Jennifer Anastasoff, executive director of the Tech Talent Project, a nonpartisan nonprofit that helps U.S. federal and state governments recruit technology leaders, made the case in an interview with StateScoop. She said artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and major changes to federal benefits programs are putting additional pressure on government systems. Incoming state and federal leaders will need to recruit experienced technologists and give existing employees the resources to modernize how government operates, she said. Anastasoff is a founding team member of the U.S. Digital Service.

Anastasoff said 36 states held gubernatorial elections this year, and incoming governors should prioritize technology-fluent leadership across their cabinets, including chief information officers, chief data officers and potentially chief AI officers. She said agency leaders do not necessarily need to be technology experts themselves, but need enough understanding to make informed decisions and access to trusted advisers. She said states are preparing for new Medicaid and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program requirements under H.R. 1 while managing cybersecurity threats and aging technology infrastructure. The Trump administration recently announced an optional six-month hold harmless period through June 30, 2027, allowing states to delay disenrolling or denying Medicaid coverage over new work requirements originally set to take effect on Jan 1. The Tech Talent Project recommends each state needs a dedicated data analyst embedded in state Medicaid agencies so beneficiaries do not lose access and caseworkers do not get backlogged.

Anastasoff said AI adoption requires more than hiring a chief AI officer, and governments need software engineers, data specialists, product managers and user experience experts who can evaluate whether AI-generated information is accurate and appropriate for public services. She said governments need people with the expertise to see where AI is real confident and real wrong. She said attracting those workers requires governments to rethink how they recruit, and while public-sector salaries may not compete with private industry, many technologists are motivated by public service. She said the bigger challenge is making sure qualified candidates can find positions and move through hiring processes quickly, and she urged incoming administrations to review job descriptions, recruitment systems and internal promotion opportunities early in their terms. She said many people reach out directly to say they are thinking about government, and the question is how effectively and how quickly they can be connected with the right role.

A recent report by the National Association of State Chief Information Officers found that many state AI officials lack the staffing, funding and authority needed to manage the technology across government agencies. The report found that while AI oversight has become a priority for state technology offices, establishing an AI leadership position is only the first step. The report states that when NASCIO first started tracking in 2023, less than 20 percent of states had a state chief artificial intelligence officer or a similar title. It states that just three years later, at least 46 states have identified at least one person tasked with directing artificial intelligence, and by its count 25 states have someone with AI in their title. Anastasoff said without investment, outdated systems and inefficient processes could continue to burden both government employees and residents who depend on public services.

In the Scottish Parliament on Wednesday, SNP MSP Zen Ghani asked what plans the Government had to use artificial intelligence to improve decision-making and increase efficiency as part of its public service reform agenda. Cabinet Secretary for Public Service Reform Ivan McKee said AI was being used to support human workers, not replace them, but confirmed the technology was being used to redesign services. He said public service reform is about redesigning services around people's needs, and digital services, data and technology is a key enabler through a dedicated work stream within the public service reform strategy. He said the government is scaling intelligent automation across core government and key public bodies, including identifying opportunities to pilot AI technology in public sector processes.

He said within the Scottish Government it is scaling responsible and ethical AI and automation, including the rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot premium and developing AI agents to reduce administrative burden and support better decision-making while retaining professional judgement. Ghani pointed to figures from Skills Development Scotland which found that while 87% of businesses in Scotland now use AI in their daily practices, 74% of businesses reported no change to staff headcount. He asked how the Scottish Government intends to ensure AI is used to streamline governance and not as a tool to replace workers. McKee said the approach is to use AI to support the workforce, reducing routine administration and freeing staff to focus on what requires human judgement, expertise and empathy.

He said responsible adoption is supported by guidance in the Digital Scotland Service Manual, transparency through the mandatory Scottish AI register, and developing an AI ethics and assurance framework alongside safeguards on data protection and security, responsible procurement and investment in AI skills. Tory MSP Craig Hoy asked if the Scottish Government was considering replacing ministers with AI given how poor some are at answering questions, particularly the Cabinet Secretary for Transport, Stephen Flynn. McKee responded that this comes from a party that used AI to generate thousands upon thousands of irrelevant, trivial questions to the Government, running up an enormous bill. Douglas Lumsden, the former Tory MSP who became an MP in the Aberdeen South by-election after Flynn was elected to Holyrood, submitted around 1000 written questions to the Scottish Government in January 2025, reportedly costing around £100 each to answer, and the SNP accused Lumsden of costing the taxpayer £100k by using AI to ask nonsense questions about bees, straws and pepper sachets.

stories.Headline: Valor Energy completes Glorious Star purchase and plans $700 million Youngstown AI data center buildout
stories.Summary:
Valor Energy Inc. completed its purchase of Glorious Star, LLC, the Ohio limited liability company that owns an operational 18 MW computing center in Youngstown, Ohio, the company announced. The deal was structured as an equity acquisition and transfers 100% of the target's equity interests to Valor Energy. Glorious Star, LLC becomes a wholly-owned subsidiary of Valor Energy after the closing. Closing came after the company completed legal, financial and technical due diligence on the target. The purchase was announced on November 17, 2026, in a report by Ashish Joshi.

The Youngstown Project comprises a facility of approximately 30,888 square feet with roughly 18 megavolt-amperes of site-level apparent power capacity. That power is delivered by Ohio Edison through an existing 23kV utility interconnection, which the Company believes is approved and energized. Valor Energy plans total investment of approximately USD 700 million, deployed in phases as the project is built out. The first phase is expected to total approximately USD 200 million, and the figures do not represent committed funding. Valor Energy Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed company trading under the symbol VAI, and Green Energy Capital Asset Inc. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.

Dave Nichols, Strategic Advisor to Valor Energy Inc., said the existing utility interconnection carrying approximately 18 MVA may reduce certain development requirements relative to starting from an undeveloped site. Nichols cautioned that conversion into an AI data center will require further development work, permits and approvals, equipment and financing. He said the Company intends to pursue that development while evaluating the project's technical requirements and commercial feasibility. Nichols said closing the acquisition is an important step in pursuing Valor Energy's AI data center strategy. He added that the Company looks forward to building the project out with the local community and creating long-term value for shareholders.

Guy Coviello, president and CEO of the Youngstown/Warren Regional Chamber, called the investment a strong vote of confidence in Youngstown and the Mahoning Valley. Coviello described the site as an ideal location for a data center, noting it has operated as a heavy industrial site for decades. He said the building is largely out of sight of residential areas and the project offers a chance to reinvest in an established industrial site. Coviello said the project could help stabilize the surrounding neighborhood, create construction jobs for the skilled trades and generate new business for local companies. The Verge reported on November 18, 2026, that AI data center projects are continuing to pop up across the US with frequent opposition from locals concerned about their impact.

The Verge cited FOX 13 News reporting that data center regulation bills are coming, according to Utah's House Speaker. The Johnson County Post asked whether a small Johnson County town should ban data centers, and voters will decide. KDFW FOX 4 reported that a Red Oak data center expansion was approved despite community pushback. The Seattle Times reported that a proposed Amazon data center near Tri-Cities gets pushback from residents. Valor Energy historically ran automobile transaction and related services businesses and is now pursuing a strategic transformation into digital infrastructure, energy and other growth sectors.

Valor Energy said it intends to work closely with local officials and community partners in Youngstown on its proposed development plans. The Company stressed that its preliminary estimates remain subject to further planning, technical assessment and the availability of financing on acceptable terms. Valor Energy stated there can be no assurance it will obtain the financing necessary for any phase of the planned development. Timing, scope and the amount of each phase will depend on further design and engineering work, required permits and approvals, construction and equipment availability, project progress, financing and market conditions. The Company added that no phase is assured of completion within an anticipated timeframe, or at all.

stories.Headline: Legora adds Teams legal intake and Microsoft 365 AI search
stories.Summary:
Legora added legal request intake in Microsoft Teams and AI search across Outlook and Calendar to its Microsoft 365 offering, and the features are now generally available, IT Brief Australia reported on 20 November 2026. Staff can submit legal requests by tagging @Legora in Teams, while lawyers can search relevant email and meeting context from Microsoft 365 as they prepare responses and next steps. Existing user permissions remain in place when lawyers use the tools. The update expands Legora's existing Microsoft integrations, which include SharePoint, OneDrive and a plug-in for Copilot for Legal. It is intended to reduce the time legal teams spend gathering background material from chats, inboxes, calendars and documents before they can begin substantive work.

Legora's Teams intake tool allows a request to begin in the collaboration platform and flow into its legal workflow, and lawyers can then use the Microsoft 365 search function within Legora to identify relevant emails and calendar information linked to the matter. Lawyers can use that context to help draft a response and prepare follow-up actions, and check source material as needed. Legora's SharePoint integration remains in beta and allows the system to use stored documents to support agreement review and save edits back to SharePoint as a new version. Its plug-in for Copilot for Legal is generally available and allows users to begin legal work from Microsoft 365 Copilot. Legora said its products are used by more than 140,000 legal professionals at more than 2,500 law firms and in-house legal teams across more than 80 markets.

Max Junestrand, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Legora, said legal work is shifting from executing tasks to directing them and standing behind the results. He said that only holds up if requests arrive with context and stay inside the controls legal teams already trust. He said that with Microsoft, Legora is making that possible, so legal professionals can spend more of their time on the judgment their stakeholders depend on them for. Tom Quoroll, Partner at Linklaters, said ensuring that its use of AI enhances the quality that Linklaters' clients expect is central to its strategy. Quoroll said Legora's integration with the wealth of Microsoft 365 context transforms its lawyers' ability to leverage that data, and that Linklaters is excited to connect two of the most powerful tools in its technology stack.

Samer Abu-Ltaif, President, Microsoft EMEA, said Legora is a great example of the bold AI innovation changing how legal work gets done, and that Microsoft is proud to help bring its solutions to lawyers around the world. He said Microsoft's customers want AI that works where they already work, and that Legora helps legal teams move from intake to finished work with relevant organizational context, ensuring enterprise security and governance. He said it is a clear example of how Microsoft's partner ecosystem turns AI into real impact. Linklaters, which uses the software, said the integration could help its lawyers make more direct use of information held within Microsoft 365. In practice, legal requests often reach in-house teams and law firms through several channels at once, including chat messages, emails and meetings, and supporting material may then sit across Outlook inboxes, calendar entries and document libraries, requiring lawyers to re-enter requests, forward files or create copies in separate systems.

Profound announced Profound for Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365, together with new integrations that connect Your AI Marketer in Profound to SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook and Microsoft Work IQ, GlobeNewswire reported from New York on 19 November 2026. By mentioning @Profound in a channel or messaging it directly, teams can ask what changed in their AI Search visibility, accuracy and citation share, why it changed, and what to do about it. From the same Teams message, they can create and run agents or start a new Profound Project, then use the Open project button to jump directly to the work, and they can also open direct-message conversations in Profound to continue working there. Your AI Marketer in Profound can find and read files in SharePoint and OneDrive, create and edit Word and Excel documents, bring selected SharePoint content into a Profound Knowledge Base and Context Manager, read email and write drafts in the connected user's Outlook mailbox, send completed reports from Outlook, and draw on a user's Microsoft 365 work context through Microsoft Work IQ. Everything Profound produces is reviewed and approved by the team before it goes live.

James Cadwallader, CEO and Co-founder of Profound, said marketing teams should not have to leave the conversation to get an answer or get work moving. He said Microsoft 365 is where much of that work already happens, so building on it was the natural choice, and that Your AI Marketer in Profound sits alongside the team, works from the content they already have and hands back results where they will be used. Sujeet Meha, VP of Teams Engineering, Microsoft, said AI is most useful when people can put it to work in the tools they already rely on. He said Profound's integration with Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 gives marketing teams a way to connect their AI marketing workflows with the conversations, documents and information they use every day, and that it is a practical example of how companies can extend Microsoft 365 to help people get more done. Profound for Microsoft Teams is available now to customers with an active Profound subscription and can be installed directly from the Microsoft Marketplace.

stories.Headline: Anthropic goes public at a $2 trillion valuation as investors demand rapid sales growth to offset huge computing costs
stories.Summary:
Anthropic began trading as a public company on November 19, 2026, opening at $111.50 a share, a 34% jump from its IPO price, and closing 17% higher at $97.17 a share. The debut gave the AI giant a $2 trillion valuation at market open, which CNN described as passing its first trading test with flying colors. The company, founded just under six years ago, is set for the largest stock market debut of all time. Its early bet on building AI tools for businesses made it a favorite of the AI market and set the stage for the record-breaking listing. As a public company, Anthropic will face more pressure to grow each quarter and prove its Claude AI agent keeps growing fast despite skyrocketing computing costs and increased competition.

Investors will look for massive sales growth each quarter to offset the nearly trillion-dollar computing expenses the company expects in the years ahead. The enterprise AI market grew fourfold in a year, from $33 billion in 2025 to $177 billion in 2026, according to Menlo Ventures, which has invested billions in Anthropic. Some businesses that fueled its rise are starting to slow their AI spending, according to one economist who monitors AI enterprise spending. Ken Mahoney, president of financial planning firm Mahoney Asset Management, said the shift is not easy, describing the move from hardly any scrutiny to analysts reevaluating everything you do.

CNN noted that the world's largest publicly traded AI companies, Nvidia, Google and Amazon, have seen their shares stumble even when quarterly numbers fall in line with Wall Street's expectations. The billions spent on infrastructure, rapid model development and growing adoption have set sky-high expectations across the industry. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei appeared on video outside the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on the day of the listing. More to follow.

stories.Headline: The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation pledges 350 million dollars in computing spending to CoreWeave
stories.Summary:
The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation will provide 350 million dollars in computing spending to the company known as CoreWeave. This financial commitment was revealed in recent tax disclosures from the charitable organization established by the former Nvidia chief executive officer. A filing from Nvidia in June identified CoreWeave as the receiver and noted that 108.3 million dollars were already spent. The funding supports the Computing Initiative for Open Science to give researchers access to large scale GPU computing resources. This specific pledge represents the largest donation made by the Huang Foundation during the 2025 calendar year.

The foundation gave 19 million dollars to the California College of the Arts and 1.2 million dollars to the Hong Kong University. Core Scientific is building a 100 megawatt data center at Port Muskogee, Oklahoma, under a broader 500 megawatt hosting agreement. This wider arrangement with CoreWeave has a potential value of 8.7 billion dollars over twelve years with two five year extensions. The Muskogee site uses 70 megawatts for critical IT capacity and 30 megawatts for cooling and electrical systems. Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company serves as the electricity provider for this facility which began construction in early 2025.

CoreWeave stated that the charitable foundation does not directly use the computing power provided through these specific financial grants. The foundation is responsible for awarding resources to scientific research grant awardees who then utilize the large scale GPU computing. Core Scientific manages the Muskogee project with Evans General Contractors serving as the construction manager under a cost plus fee contract. The project design includes two compute data halls and one separate network data hall to accommodate high density GPU equipment. These facilities will support high performance computing workloads for CoreWeave and one end customer who remains undisclosed to the public.

Investors are scrutinizing the financial interactions between AI infrastructure firms and consumers because the sector is now heavily financially intertwined. CoreWeave investors view the foundation pledge as a sign of more demand for computing services and the necessary GPU hardware. Port Muskogee estimates the data center will generate 4 billion dollars in capital investment and 182 million dollars in benefits. Local entities including Muskogee County, the City of Muskogee, and Hilldale School District may receive 12 million dollars in tax revenue. The project is expected to support 150 jobs with average salaries that exceed 65,000 dollars for the local workforce.

The foundation assets were 12.7 billion dollars at December 31, 2025, which is an increase from the previous 9.2 billion dollars. About 90 percent of these assets consist of Nvidia shares, and the organization gave 373 million dollars in 2024. CoreWeave relies on powerful GPUs for its cloud computing company, and Nvidia is a key stakeholder in the business. This expansion is part of a wider US buildout, including Oracle's 165 billion dollar Project Jupiter planned for New Mexico. Core Scientific is converting and developing infrastructure to serve the growing demand for AI and cloud computing across the country.

The Muskogee facility was initially anticipated to reach substantial completion during the first half of the 2026 calendar year. Investors will continue to scrutinize future disclosures regarding the remaining computing obligations and the revenue contributions for the firm CoreWeave. The articles do not identify the specific end customer who will use the GPU infrastructure at the Oklahoma data center. They also leave open the specific types of AI workloads that are planned for the Muskogee high performance computing facility. No further details are provided regarding the exact timing of the remaining payments from the Huang Foundation to CoreWeave.

stories.Headline: Meta rethinks its 2030 net-zero deadline as 2025 emissions rise 45%
stories.Summary:
Meta Platforms posted its 2026 Sustainability Report on Thursday, November 19, 2026, and said it is rethinking the 2030 deadline for its net-zero goal. The report said Meta's 2025 net emissions rose to 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, up 45% from 2024. Meta's stock closed Friday, November 20, at $560.84, down 5.93%, during a broad tech selloff. Shares fell 11.6% over the past week, then traded at $569.32 after hours. Meta set the goal in 2020: net zero across its whole value chain, plus water positive, by 2030.

Meta says it matched 100% of its electricity with clean and renewable energy for the sixth straight year. Direct Scope 1 emissions were just 33,555 tons, and market-based Scope 2 purchased power was 10,861 tons. Scope 3 amounted to 11,858,913 tons, about 99% of the total. Capital goods such as servers, chips, networking gear, steel and concrete made up 73%, and clean power contracts do little to reduce them. By the article's calculation, electricity use rose 34.9% to 24,849,122 megawatt-hours, and data centers used 24,523,035 of that.

Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability, wrote in the report's opening letter that Meta is "re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones." They said AI demand grew faster than almost anyone projected, and clean energy fell behind because of years-long grid interconnection waiting lines, slow permitting, and lagging transmission. Meta says its long-term dreams are unchanged, but it gave no date for a revised plan. Mark Zuckerberg spoke on the October 21, 2026 earnings call and said Muse is "very compute-intensive to run" and that "we have not launched it globally yet." Third-quarter capex was $34.906 billion, up 85.38%, and free cash flow was -$2.120 billion.

Alphabet, Google's parent company, faces the same pressure, having pledged in 2020 to run on carbon-free energy by 2030. Google stopped saying carbon-neutral operations by 2024 and has acknowledged that its emissions are still rising. By the article's math, 2025 Scope 3 was about 2.05 times the 5,772,583-ton 2021 baseline Meta aims not to exceed by end-2031. Reaching it would require cleaner suppliers or slower building. The climate reset adds some image and regulatory exposure, and the bigger question for the stock is whether the expansion pays off.

Meta still guides 2026 capex to $135 billion to $145 billion. Third-quarter revenue rose 26.07%, and the stock trades at a P/E of 21, which the article calls reasonable for that growth. For comparison, Alphabet already shows AI spending turning into sales, as Google Cloud revenue rose 103%. The interconnection waiting lines and permitting delays that slowed clean energy also limit how fast new data centers can come online. The article says the core business is paying for the expansion so far.

The test for this view is Meta's fourth-quarter call, where it will give 2027 capex guidance. If capex rises again while fourth-quarter revenue comes in below the $73 billion low end of guidance, the case for the expansion weakens. The articles leave open what a revised net-zero plan would contain, since Meta gave no date for one. They also leave open whether cleaner suppliers or slower building could bring Scope 3 back to the 2021 baseline by end-2031. Whether the expansion pays off remains the bigger question the articles say the stock faces.

stories.Headline: Nvidia invests 58.1 billion dollars in AI companies amid booming revenue growth
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reported its third quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17, showing a massive boom in its artificial intelligence business. The company achieved revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, which represents a 103 percent increase compared to the previous year. This financial report was the first one released without Jensen Huang serving as the chief executive officer of the firm. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress announced that the company is continuing to ship its next generation platform. The company also confirmed that the roadmap for its Vera Rubin technology remains on track for future development and release.

The data center business generated 107.6 billion dollars, while the company expects fourth quarter revenue of approximately 130 billion dollars. Nvidia spent 58.1 billion dollars on other AI companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, during nine months ending October 25. The firm provided 105 billion dollars in credit support for the PORTS-Pike data center project in Ohio for OpenAI. Total credit guarantees reached 118 billion dollars, and future commitments to neocloud firms totaled 32 billion dollars in the quarter. The company also spent 61.2 billion dollars on stock buybacks, which is up from 36.3 billion dollars last year.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that returning value to shareholders is a super top priority for the current management team. She noted that the company intends to use its remaining 227.3 billion dollar buyback authorization by the end of 2028. Kress explained that providing capital assistance to suppliers is another priority to ensure they can build more infrastructure quickly. Regarding customer data centers, she said the company must deeply analyze the strength of plans before making any investments. She also clarified that some credit guarantees vanish if construction is delayed or if customers face building challenges.

James Kisner of Water Tower Research warned that Nvidia is double exposed if the artificial intelligence spending boom eventually slows. He suggested that the company might be fueling its own demand by investing billions into its own customer base. This strategy affects the broader AI ecosystem, including frontier labs, infrastructure financiers, and various private companies receiving Nvidia capital. Investors are affected by a valuation reset, as shares fell 6.95 percent to 135.83 dollars on a recent Friday. The company's total market valuation dropped to 3.7 trillion dollars as of November 18, down from 5 trillion dollars.

Nvidia ended 2013 with a price to earnings ratio of 19.6, which was higher than its current ratio. Historical benchmarks show the multiple was 18.3 in 2014 and 17.1 in 2018, both above the current level. The current trailing price to earnings ratio is 15.68, while the forward ratio is 9.24 and PEG is 0.178. Net income more than doubled to 65.3 billion dollars from 31.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share hit 2.70. Equity securities generated 1.8 billion dollars in net gains, though this included a 1 billion dollar non-marketable loss.

The company will monitor data center growth and gross margins to see if the lower valuation represents a real opportunity. Management will continue to evaluate whether financing select customer data centers is the right type of investment for the firm. The outlook for the next quarter assumes that Nvidia will receive no data center compute revenue from China. It remains open whether Wall Street is too cautious or if competition will intensify and slow down infrastructure spending. Investors must now watch if customers become more selective with capital investments as the AI spending boom continues.
