stories.Headline: Indian firms cut entry-level tech hiring 44% while planning 45,000 fresher hires
stories.Summary:
General Assembly published research showing that many Learning and Development leaders believe AI is weakening employees' human skills, IT Brief Australia reported on 19 November 2026. The study surveyed 510 HR and Learning and Development leaders at large companies across six countries. More than half of respondents, 52%, said AI use is degrading skills such as communication, conflict resolution and collaboration. Another 41% said ensuring employees retain or develop critical thinking, communication and other soft skills despite using AI will be one of their biggest challenges in the coming year. The findings highlight a tension inside large organisations as companies expand AI training while trying to preserve workplace skills that are harder to automate.

At the same time, 83% of respondents said human skills are becoming more valued within their organisations, and 59% expect demand for soft skills training to rise. Nearly two-thirds, 64%, said their teams are under pressure to deliver AI upskilling across the workforce. AI literacy was most often ranked as the top skill Learning and Development teams themselves will need. One-third of respondents, 33%, said closing the AI skills gap is a leading challenge, while 31% pointed to change management and employee fatigue around AI. The research found that 57% of leaders expect demand for role-specific AI training to grow, while 56% expect their organisations to expand personalised learning journeys, 55% expect more hands-on training and 52% expect more job-based or role-based training.

Out-of-the-box third-party training was the option most likely to be deprioritised, with 15% of organisations expecting to place less emphasis on it. Daniele Grassi, Chief Executive Officer of General Assembly, said employers are trying to balance technical training with broader workplace development. He said Learning and Development professionals are tasked with building role-specific AI skills while making sure the human skills that matter most do not erode in the process. He said companies are increasingly looking to integrate AI and soft skills training to prepare employees for the future of work. He said training is becoming more hands-on, with opportunities to practice critical thinking, judgement and collaboration alongside AI usage and get feedback in real time.

Among respondents who said their learning strategy is fully linked to documented business priorities, 23% expect a significant budget increase, compared with 11% of other respondents. The same pattern appeared among leaders who said they work closely with functional heads to map future skills needs and among those who said they help shape business strategy. More broadly, 73% said company leadership regularly asks for Learning and Development input on workforce capability, transformation or future skills decisions, while 63% said Learning and Development leaders help shape business strategy. Connecting learning initiatives to business outcomes or return on investment was the second most-cited challenge for the coming year, named by 35% of respondents. Less than half, 47%, said business outcomes such as revenue growth or profit are among their top three measures of success.

By contrast, 36% still count course completions among their leading metrics, and 26% said distinguishing AI course completions from actual competency is a major challenge. Half of respondents in dedicated Learning and Development roles said course completions are a top metric, compared with 32% of those in broader HR roles who also oversee training. Grassi said the pressure to show results is growing as organisations spend more on AI-related learning. He said businesses are investing in AI upskilling, but the big challenge for Learning and Development leaders is proving that what they are doing is working. He said that means going beyond counting how many people took a course, and measuring behaviour changes, skills and competencies instead, and linking those to real business outcomes.

Avi Patchava, CEO (joint) of Bright Money, wrote in ETCIO on 14 November 2026 that entry-level tech openings were down 44% year on year by mid-2026. When ICRIER surveyed 651 IT firms, 55% said they had cut entry-level hiring, while only 14% said the same about senior roles. At Infosys, the share of employees aged 30 or under is the lowest it has been in 15 years. Nomura tracked about 83,000 AI-related hires in India against roughly 32,000 AI-linked exits, and TCS and Infosys between them still plan to take on around 45,000 freshers this year. Patchava wrote that more than 90% of Indian employees already use generative AI tools, and that in 2017 he ran a research study with 28 successful Indian graduates at McKinsey India.

stories.Headline: LG Electronics promotes 44 executives and forms a CEO-led AI partnership team to speed AI and robotics growth
stories.Summary:
LG Electronics announced on November 19, 2026, that it promoted 44 executives and reshuffled its leadership to improve its competitive edge during the AI era. The company created a new AI partnership team that reports directly to CEO Lyu Jae-cheol to strengthen ties with global tech firms. These changes aim to accelerate growth in future businesses such as robotics, mobility, smart factories, and data center cooling. The organizational restructuring will take effect on December 1, while the executive promotions become official on January 1.

The reshuffle includes promoting Baek Seung-tae, the head of the home appliance business, and Lee Sang-woo, the head of management strategy at LG Corp, to presidents. Lee Sang-woo will now lead the TV and display business, while Baek Seung-tae continues to manage home appliances and robot actuator commercialization. LG Electronics is establishing a new applied business unit under its Eco Solution division to expand its data center cooling operations. Additionally, a new unit under the vehicle division will focus on advanced driver assistance systems and high-performance computing.

Company leadership stated that these moves are intended to speed up decision-making and respond more quickly to changing market conditions. To achieve this, regional heads for Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa will now report directly to the CEO. The company is also leveraging a multibillion-dollar deal to supply chillers for data centers with a combined capacity of 5 gigawatts. LG Electronics aims to reach 1 trillion won in annual chiller sales as early as next year.

To support this growth, the company plans to establish a manufacturing subsidiary in Virginia next year to meet rising demand. This strategy builds on the creation of a robotics business center in July that also reports directly to the CEO. The electronics maker continues to streamline its global management structure by reducing layers between regional operations and headquarters. These efforts are part of a broader push to develop robotics and AI infrastructure into primary growth engines.

stories.Headline: Police in Seoul continue investigating alleged AI cheating by perfect LEET scorer Lee Jin-woo after his death
stories.Summary:
Lee Jin-woo was found dead in Seoul on Thursday, November 19, 2026. He was the first person to earn a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test. Police and fire authorities found the 32 year old man in Gangdong District. He died before a planned livestream to dispel allegations of AI assisted cheating. A short note was found, but it did not address the cheating claims.

The IDA admissions research institute planned a verification event at a Gangnam District studio. It required metal detectors and ear endoscopy checks to rule out any hidden devices. Lee would solve the Korean language section of the current College Scholastic Ability Test. The event would be livestreamed on YouTube and include a session with a language instructor. Lee had previously entered Korea University in 2024 and Seoul National University in 2026.

Police said they will continue the investigation to establish the substantive truth of the case. They assigned the matter to the financial crimes investigation team of the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. Lawyer Park Eun-sun of 2yoo law firm said it is important to uncover cheating methods. Lawyer Kwak Joon-ho of Law Firm Chung said investigations can proceed to establish the facts. Police are now seeking a forensic examination and an autopsy to determine the cause.

Lawyer Jeong Joon-yeong of HMP Law said meaningful results are difficult without a statement from Lee. Some test takers say the state is failing to manage exams properly in the AI era. A 22 year old preparing for civil service exams said national exams have lost credibility. This person mentioned the tax accountant cheating case and the LEET case as examples. Others view the failure to appear at the verification as a tacit admission of guilt.

Lee once placed in the sixth to eighth tiers on the national college entrance exam. He later claimed to have developed his own study method to improve his scores. He faced allegations that his sharp improvement resulted from using artificial intelligence during his tests. Some claimed he received suspicious private tutoring in life science just before the CSAT exam. His LEET answer sheet showed signs that he had marked answers in the wrong rows.

Police applied for an order to preserve Lee's answer booklet at Younghoon High School in Gangbuk. They want to use the booklet from last year's CSAT as evidence in the probe. Investigators are looking for any accomplices who may have helped Lee cheat on the exams. The articles leave open whether the police will find evidence without a statement from Lee. It remains unknown if the forensic examination will reveal more about his death.

Articles.Title: After LEET perfect scorer’s death, AI cheating probe faces uphill battle

stories.Headline: Korea plans unannounced exam alerts to catch AI cheaters
stories.Summary:
The government is considering sending unannounced disaster alert messages during this week's annual college entrance exam to catch cheaters using their phones and prevent cheating assisted by artificial intelligence, an interior ministry official said Wednesday. Authorities have been mulling measures to root out cheating during the College Scholastic Ability Test on Thursday following a recent cheating scandal in the certified tax accountant exam using AI. As part of anti-cheating measures unveiled Tuesday, the government said it would send an emergency alert message before the start of the exam to detect any unsubmitted devices. The official said the government is considering sending alerts unannounced in addition to the planned alert scheduled to be sent between 8:25 and 8:30 a.m. President Lee Jae Myung said Tuesday he had instructed authorities to review sending additional alerts, even during testing, to catch cheaters.

The government will send another disaster alert at an unspecified time during this week's annual college entrance exam, the interior ministry said Wednesday. While the first alert will be sent at 8:30 a.m., just before the start of the test, the ministry plans to send another message at an undisclosed time to find any test takers with unsubmitted phones. The ministry said the alerts will ring for 10.5 seconds at full volume, urging the public not to be alarmed. The education ministry notified schools nationwide Wednesday that it will allow test takers to only bring in pencils inside CSAT exam rooms, revising its list of permitted items. Authorities earlier notified test takers that they were allowed to bring black marker pens, correction tape, erasers, pencils and mechanical pencil lead for the exam, and under the revised rules, stationery items except for pencils will be provided at the test sites.

President Lee Jae Myung called on officials Tuesday to thoroughly prepare anti-cheating measures for the nationwide college entrance exam set to take place this week, describing cheating as a grave crime that undermines social trust. Lee made the remarks during an emergency meeting to inspect the country's readiness for the CSAT, also known in Korean as Suneung, scheduled for Thursday, following widespread concerns over cheating using AI. Lee said the Suneung is a symbol of fairness and a ladder of opportunity in our society during a video meeting held from Manila, as he wrapped up his visit to the city for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. Lee added that officials must take strict action against those who engage in misconduct, adhering to a zero-tolerance policy, while asking them to come up with response measures against AI-assisted cheating. In a subsequent social media post, Lee said the government plans to offer a reward of over 100 million won, or US$74,805, per case to those who report instances of cheating involving advanced gadgets, should the case be confirmed.

Anti-cheating measures announced earlier Tuesday include physically checking all glasses worn by test takers, covering buttons on their clothes with stickers and blocking Wi-Fi networks inside and near the test sites. The government also warned that test takers caught cheating will be banned from the CSAT for the next 10 years, while facing criminal punishment. The move appears to reflect concerns of misconduct involving miniature cameras hidden inside personal items brought by test takers. South Korea has recently been rocked by the recent confession of the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam that he had cheated with the help of AI and digital devices.

The incident has deepened worries of such cheating on the upcoming CSAT, widely seen as a major life event in South Korea, where the university one goes to can heavily influence career prospects. The anti-cheating measures were unveiled Tuesday, and the education ministry notified schools nationwide Wednesday of the revised permitted items list. The first alert will be sent at 8:30 a.m. just before the start of the test, while the planned alert was scheduled to be sent between 8:25 and 8:30 a.m.

The interior ministry official said that if the time is known, there would effectively be no point in additional alerts. President Lee made his remarks during a video meeting held from Manila, as he wrapped up his visit to the city for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. The CSAT, also known in Korean as Suneung, is scheduled for Thursday. The government is considering sending alerts unannounced in addition to the planned alert, and the ministry plans to send another message at an undisclosed time to find any test takers with unsubmitted phones.

The ministry said the alerts will ring for 10.5 seconds at full volume, urging the public not to be alarmed. Under the revised rules, stationery items except for pencils will be provided at the test sites. The government plans to offer a reward of over 100 million won per case to those who report instances of cheating involving advanced gadgets, should the case be confirmed. Test takers caught cheating will be banned from the CSAT for the next 10 years, while facing criminal punishment.

stories.Headline: Sitespace co-CEO Lee Ju-yeon demonstrates smart glasses at Seoul education office training for CSAT staff
stories.Summary:
Lee Ju-yeon, co-CEO of the nonprofit startup Sitespace, is the woman shown wearing black smart glasses and looking at a test paper in recent articles about exam cheating using artificial intelligence glasses. The photo was taken on the 11th at the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education in Yongsan-gu, Seoul, during a training session for dedicated smart-glasses headquarters staff for the College Scholastic Ability Test. Sitespace had first contacted the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education to propose introducing the functions of smart glasses, which led to the event. At the training, they demonstrated functions such as taking photos with smart glasses, solving test questions, and communicating with a smartphone. Reporters flocked in to film the demonstration, and photos of Lee appeared in multiple outlets after suspicions emerged on the 12th about cheating with smart glasses by the top scorer in the tax accountant exam.

The session taught staff assigned to test sites in Seoul about the features of smart glasses and how to identify them. Co-CEO Jeong Jin-seorang said they first went to show the actual glasses to supervisors at the education office, and after they asked that teachers also be allowed to handle them directly, it turned into a training session. The other woman photographed with Lee was a practicum guide hired short-term for the day's training. Sitespace assisted with smart-glasses identification at test sites on the 19th, the day of the CSAT, identifying models by checking photos sent by the education authorities when a device suspected of being smart glasses was found. A smart-glasses identification aid app developed by Sitespace, which detects nearby Bluetooth and Wi-Fi signals and helps determine whether glasses are AI-enabled based on photos taken from multiple angles, was also used by CSAT proctors.

Lee said in a phone call with Kyunghyang Shinmun on the 19th that AI glasses can be used for public-interest purposes as well, but it seemed like public opinion was becoming too negative. She said they told the education office they wished to explain the functions of the glasses free of charge for the public good. Lee said she was there for work, so she wore comfortable clothes with no makeup, and she did not expect reporters to come. She said that because the proctor teachers have portrait rights issues, she told them it would be better to photograph us doing the demonstration instead. Lee said that at first she was flustered, but now she thinks she has come to enjoy it a bit, and that she is glad many people have learned that there are AI-glasses services like ours engaged in public-interest work.

Jeong recalled that she finished a lecture for teachers in the basement auditorium and came upstairs, and Lee was surrounded by cameras firing flashes like a movie scene. They said they had attended without knowing the event would be open to the press. After the articles ran, people with visual impairments and related institutions reportedly inquired about trying out the app. Jeong said they received many identification requests, but most turned out to be ordinary glasses.

According to the Ministry of Education, one case of cheating using smart glasses during the exam was uncovered that day at a CSAT test site in South Chungcheong Province. Sitespace launched after winning the top prize in April at the startup competition of Hongik University, the alma mater of the two co-founders. Jeong said they at first envisioned a docent service in museums based on smart glasses, but after meeting many people with visual impairments, they realized what was truly needed was technology that helps with mobility. Sitespace is developing an app that uses the cameras and speakers of commercially available smart glasses to provide audio guidance about the surrounding environment, recognizing objects in the user's line of sight with the camera and conveying them through sound.

Instead of long sentences, it is designed to deliver only the necessary information quickly and concisely, such as sliding door, automatic door, and half open. They are currently improving functions through pilot use. After CES 2027 in Las Vegas, USA, next January, they plan to officially release the app on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Lee said that AI glasses and ultra-miniature cameras are being used in negative ways, but technology continues to advance.

She said they want to let people know that there are organizations that use technology for the public good. The articles do not say what became of the cheating case uncovered in South Chungcheong Province. The articles do not say how the identification requests were resolved beyond most turning out to be ordinary glasses. The articles do not give the outcome of the tax accountant exam cheating suspicions.

stories.Headline: MIT and Mecalux find 57% of firms expect AI to make over a quarter of warehouse decisions autonomously by 2028
stories.Summary:
A study by the MIT Centre for Transportation & Logistics and Mecalux found that 57% of organisations expect AI to make or execute more than a quarter of warehouse operational decisions autonomously by 2028, based on a survey of nearly 2,000 supply chain and warehousing professionals across 21 countries. The report, published on 20 November 2026, examined generative and agentic AI in warehouse operations and found that 61% of organisations reported using generative AI at large-scale deployment or full integration, compared with 56% for agentic AI. About three in four deployments had been at their current stage for less than a year, yet 87% of generative AI applications and 81% of agentic AI applications showed at least moderate improvement in their target metrics. Only 39% of generative AI use cases and 36% of agentic AI use cases had significant gains that were both quantified and documented, and where respondents could estimate the scale, the typical gain was about 20% on the main target metric.

Companies are giving AI systems authority in selected areas while keeping tighter controls elsewhere, with inventory movements the area where agents were most often allowed to decide without human approval at 51% of agentic AI use cases, followed by data corrections at 42%. Only 22% of these systems were allowed to make customer-facing commitments and 12% were permitted to make financial decisions, and the most common oversight model was human-on-the-loop, in which AI operates within defined limits while employees monitor and can intervene. Organisations with comprehensive, actively enforced AI governance were about twice as likely to report significant, documented improvements, at 51% versus 26% for generative AI and 46% versus 23% for agentic AI, a pattern that held after accounting for deployment status, region, industry and budget, though the study noted association rather than proof of causation. Legacy system integration was the biggest constraint on scaling generative AI for 40% of respondents, while 54% said better integration with warehouse management and ERP systems would have the greatest effect on adoption.

Matthias Winkenbach, Director of the Intelligent Logistics Systems Lab, said the objective was to move beyond general sentiment and provide practical guidance on where these technologies deliver operational value today and where they remain experimental. Javier Carrillo, Chief Executive Officer of Mecalux, said warehouse decision-makers need AI they can measure and that the research gives clients a clear map of where the technology is working and what it takes to prove it. On employment, 56% of organisations said the technology had mainly shifted staff towards higher-value tasks, while 11% reported reduced headcount and 9% reported increased headcount, and 73% said they were upskilling warehouse-floor staff while 61% were creating new technical roles. Ninety per cent anticipated an increase in AI investment over the next two to three years, with 29% expecting that rise to exceed 25%, broadly in line with the previous year's study, and among companies that had fully integrated the technologies, 70% expected agentic AI to make or execute more than a quarter of warehouse operational decisions autonomously by 2028.

Articles.Title: Study finds AI will run more warehouse decisions by 2028 - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Korea Consumer Agency finds over half of surveyed Koreans who changed medication on AI advice suffered side effects
stories.Summary:
The Korea Consumer Agency released a survey on Thursday, November 19, 2026, showing that many Koreans suffered health problems after following medical advice from generative AI chatbots. Out of 500 adults who used AI for medicine or supplements in the past year, 110 people changed or stopped their medication without professional help. More than half of those individuals, specifically 56 people, experienced negative health consequences including worsened conditions or adverse reactions. Other findings showed that 133 respondents skipped or delayed hospital visits because they trusted the information provided by the AI services.

The survey revealed that 27.3 percent of affected users had mild reactions like indigestion, while 19.1 percent suffered treatment setbacks and 14.5 percent required additional medical care. AI tools were used most often for over the counter drugs at 76.2 percent, health supplements at 63.8 percent, and prescription drugs at 15.6 percent. Testing of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity showed that some provided medicine advice without checking age or existing health conditions. Furthermore, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude directed users to proxy purchase websites for drugs that are banned from online sales.

The Korea Consumer Agency urged AI companies to block illegal drug sites and make their medical warnings more prominent for users. OpenAI and Anthropic stated they would consider improving their warnings and information filtering, while Google said it would maintain its current system. Perplexity did not provide a response to the agency's recommendations regarding these safety concerns. The agency also warned consumers to use AI only for reference and to always consult a pharmacist or doctor before altering any medication.

Articles.Title: Half of Koreans who changed medication on AI advice suffered side effects, survey finds

stories.Headline: South Korea's personnel minister says AI will shift civil servants toward judgment and problem-solving work
stories.Summary:
South Korea's Minister of Personnel Management, Tschoe Dong-seok, said in an interview with The Korea Herald published on Nov. 19, 2026, that artificial intelligence will take over routine administrative tasks and that civil servants will increasingly be expected to exercise independent judgment, solve complex problems and engage with the public. He said the next 10 years will be a period of fundamental change in the roles of public officials and the way the civil service operates, driven by the rapid advancement of AI and other technologies. As AI takes over simple and repetitive tasks, he said, public officials will be able to concentrate more on roles that only humans can perform, such as policy judgment, solving complex problems and communicating with the public. Those changes have prompted the government to rethink how it recruits, trains and evaluates its workforce.

The Ministry of Personnel Management plans to expand the Public Service Aptitude Test, currently used for Grade 5 and Grade 7 recruitment, to Grade 9 examinations by 2029, and the new assessment is designed to evaluate logical reasoning, data analysis and decision-making abilities rather than primarily testing memorized knowledge. The government also plans to introduce the assessment to local government Grade 7 recruitment in 2027 and firefighter officer candidate examinations in 2028, while encouraging broader adoption across public institutions. The ministry is pursuing additional pay increases for junior officials in Grades 7 through 9 and discussing further improvements with fiscal authorities, aiming to bring starting salaries for Grade 9 officials to approximately 3 million won, including allowances, in 2027. For specialized AI and information technology positions, the government already offers special salary arrangements that allow compensation comparable to private-sector levels, and the ministry is expanding AI-related hiring to include computer systems development and data.

All civil servants are now required to complete at least two hours of AI training annually, supported by a government learning platform that integrates educational resources from public and private providers, and the ministry plans to expand practical training that enables officials to identify workplace problems and develop solutions using AI, alongside specialized programs for managers responsible for leading organizational transformation. Tschoe said attracting young talent would also require improvements in compensation, and he emphasized that adapting to technological change would require more than simply introducing new tools. He said government workplace culture must also move away from hierarchical management toward greater autonomy, professionalism and collaboration. The ministry introduced a continuous performance management system across government ministries in October, allowing supervisors and employees to regularly review work progress and document individual contributions, and Tschoe said the changes would improve evaluation transparency and ensure civil servants in demanding fields, including disaster response and public safety, receive greater recognition for their contributions.

He said the ultimate goal of reforming how the civil service works is not simply to improve efficiency but to enable public officials to focus on policy judgment and problem-solving for citizens and provide better public services. Tschoe's remarks came as Korea hosted the fourth annual meeting of the Asia Public Service Network in Seoul on Wednesday, bringing together representatives from 14 countries and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development to discuss the future of public administration. The conference was held under the theme "Leadership for Transformation" and focused on organizational reform, performance management and building a workforce capable of adapting to emerging technologies. Among the findings scheduled to be shared at the conference were those of a joint study South Korea and the OECD conducted from 2025 to 2026 on how participating countries use digital technologies to recruit civil servants, and further joint research and exchanges are planned.

stories.Headline: South Korea detects 111 exam cheating cases as AI fears grow
stories.Summary:
The 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test took place on Thursday, November 20, 2026, amid high anxiety over AI assisted cheating. Many students and experts now question if traditional safeguards can keep exams fair against advancing technology. The Education Ministry reported that 111 cheating cases involving smartphones and other electronic devices were detected. Some examinees attempted to cheat despite advance warnings from the Interior Ministry and the Education Ministry. These violations occurred at various testing sites, including a high school in Yeongtong District, Suwon, Gyeonggi.

The government sent three highest level emergency alert messages, including one announced in advance and two unannounced, to identify phones. These alerts sound even when devices are set to silent, and they helped uncover 54 of the cheating cases. Five cases involved the use of smart devices during the exam, while 52 others were detected through Wi-Fi signal detection. Examinees had to roll up sleeves to expose wrists and place stickers over clothing buttons, measures credited to Han Seong-sook. Proctors checked these analog measures during each session, and bags were placed in hallways to prevent the use of devices.

Vice Education Minister Choi Eun-ok briefed reporters on AI cheating cases at the Government Complex Sejong on November 19. Park Joo-ho, president of Daelim University College, stated that maintaining traditional assessment methods will only place a greater burden on examinees. He argued that the weight of the CSAT in university admissions must be reduced to ensure fairness. Park suggested that universities should evaluate applicants through a wider range of methods beyond written exams. He noted that while these changes are necessary, they would be difficult to implement for the 2028 CSAT.

Parents like 48 year old Jung Mi-seo, waiting at Duksung Girls' High School in Jongno District, Seoul, expressed deep anxiety. Jung noted her daughter wore contact lenses instead of glasses and wondered if this would be required for every exam. Seventeen year old Lee Si-yeon questioned the point of exams if people can get high scores by using AI. A 29 year old teacher surnamed Kim in Seocho District, Seoul, said students made cynical remarks about powerful AI tools. One test taker in Suwon described the exam room atmosphere as unsettling after a student was caught with a smartphone.

The tech industry doubts that current methods can catch AI cheaters as hidden devices become smarter. This year's CSAT followed a pattern of increasing concerns over whether some AI violations went undetected by proctors. The government used emergency alerts because some students failed to surrender their phones before the exam began. Traditional analog inspection methods are now being questioned for use in upcoming professional licensing exams. These events highlight a growing conflict between advancing technology and the premise that the entire testing process is fair.

The government will continue to monitor cheating as the nation considers whether traditional exam methods can still ensure fairness. Experts believe serious discussions must begin regarding the reform of assessment methods to combat technological advances. It remains open whether analog checks, like stickers on buttons, will be applied to other national examinations. The industry continues to doubt the effectiveness of current security measures against smarter hidden devices. It is unclear if the admissions system will be reformed in time for the 2028 CSAT.

stories.Headline: Han Won-seok admits to using AI to cheat on a national exam as Seoul officials propose phasing out Suneung by 2040
stories.Summary:
Han Won-seok recently admitted to using a smartphone, a miniature camera, and generative artificial intelligence to achieve the highest score on a national tax accountant exam. This admission occurred as over half a million students prepared to take the College Scholastic Ability Test, known as Suneung, on Thursday, November 19, 2026. The scandal has sparked wider concerns about AI-assisted cheating on other high-stakes tests, including the Legal Education Eligibility Test and civil service exams. Government officials have launched a broad investigation into various national qualification exams held throughout the current year.

The ruling Democratic Party is now pursuing legislation that would impose a ten-year ban on any test-taker caught cheating with artificial intelligence. Meanwhile, the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education is pushing a December 2025 roadmap that suggests starting systemic changes in 2028. This specific plan proposes a shift toward essay-based assessments and the complete phaseout of the Suneung by the 2040 academic year. Such a transition would move the primary responsibility for assessing applicants away from a national exam and into the hands of individual universities.

Park Do-soon, the first director of the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation, stated that written exams only test about one-tenth of curricular goals. He argued that the current system is limited because it asks questions that artificial intelligence can easily answer. Similarly, Korea University professor Cho Byeok has called for the total abolition of the Suneung to reduce the knowledge burden on students. Cho predicted that the national education system will undergo major changes within the next five years.

The government has pledged zero tolerance for cheating, but critics argue that simply removing devices from rooms does not solve the underlying problem. The debate now focuses on whether traditional written exams can still accurately measure a student's actual abilities in an AI-driven world. While the Seoul education office has provided a concrete timetable for retirement, the national government has not yet adopted the proposal. Future efforts may focus on giving students more opportunities to demonstrate their reasoning through written work.

stories.Headline: South Korea's top tax exam scorer admits using AI to cheat, casting doubt on CPA exam fairness
stories.Summary:
In South Korea, people who passed the certified public accountant exam are facing a tighter job market and new doubts about exam fairness, after the top scorer in this year's certified tax accountant exam admitted using generative artificial intelligence and electronic devices to cheat, The Korea Times reported on Nov. 20, 2026. The same person confessed to using those methods during the CPA exam, though he did not pass it, and he appeared before reporters at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. A candidate who spent at least three years preparing and missed the passing score by less than a point said it felt deeply unfair that people who played by the rules were paying the price. He added that if the top scorer had not admitted to cheating, candidates might never have realized they had been denied a fair shot.

Passing the CPA exam does not by itself qualify a candidate to practice, because under the Certified Public Accountant Act each passer must first complete a year of practical training at an approved institution such as an accounting firm, a public corporation or a private company. As of September, 723 passers had yet to register with a training institution, according to the Korean Accounting Association. The annual quota has already been lowered twice, from 1,250 in 2024 to 1,200 in 2025 and 1,150 in 2026, and expectations are growing that it will be cut by another 50 places next year. The Financial Services Commission is expected to set the minimum number of candidates that can be selected from next year's exam by the end of November.

The Financial Supervisory Service, which administers the CPA exam, said it would work with experts and relevant institutions to develop measures to prevent cheating using sophisticated electronic devices. In a study released Nov. 4, researchers at the Korean Accounting Association estimated that AI adoption could reduce accounting firms' demand for audit staff by about 10 percent over the next three to five years, with the decline reaching 12 to 16 percent thereafter, and they proposed reducing the annual quota by as many as 300 over the next two to three years. A 30-year-old accountant at a major entertainment company said she was glad to have found a job before AI took off, though she doubts demand for junior staff will hold up over time. The scandal has unsettled people still studying for the exams as well as those who have already passed, raising questions about whether the exam's safeguards are keeping pace with advanced technology.

Articles.Title: Aspiring accountants face tougher odds as AI reshapes hiring, shakes confidence in CPA exam

stories.Headline: Lenexa Medical wins three VIC AI Awards including Best in Australia
stories.Summary:
Lenexa Medical, a Victorian health technology startup, won three prizes at the VIC AI Awards 2026 in Melbourne, where it was named Best Use of AI in Healthcare, AI Startup of the Year and Best in Australia, the awards recognising projects across technical and creative artificial intelligence categories with winners drawn from Victoria, elsewhere in Australia and overseas. The company was the biggest winner on the technical side of the program through its LenexaCARE product, and it has also been recognised by TIME Magazine as one of the world's top Health Technology companies. Other technical winners included Rostrum AI, which took the Best Enterprise AI Tool award for RostrumLink with Orato, and SPQR Technologies, which won Best AI for Safety for Aegis Runtime Control: Independent Execution Authority for AI Agents. The creative awards covered art, film, music and advertising made with AI tools, with Annelise (Wink.) Clark winning Best in AI Art for Cul-de-Sac Couture and the Best AI Campaign/Commercial prize going to Chapel Street Precinct Film, created by Toby Goodman and the team at CoastGen.

In the film categories, Glamourexia by John Paul DeFazio won Best in AI Short Films, while Edmond Yang took Best in AI Animation for When You Run From Your Mom, and the Best AI Music / Music Videos award went to Is This Not real? by Jason Joseph Dainter. A special Rising Star award went to Peek-a-Boo! A Bunny's Halloween Night, directed by Guillaume Descamps. Matt Kirby, Director of the VIC AI Awards and VIC AI Boom, said the quality of entries stood out before judging began, noting that submissions came from local Victorian individuals and companies alongside international ones and that startups without a profile yet sometimes blew the judges away.

He also pointed to the commercial focus of the technical category winners, saying they are all driven by a real-world need and that it is easy to fall in love with the power of AI but there must be a worthwhile outcome for it to stack up commercially. Kirby said two of the winning filmmakers showed how AI-assisted work could still rely on traditional storytelling strengths, saying both know how to tell a story and that AI is supporting their ideas but it is still driven by human emotion and creativity. The winners reflected a mix of Victorian startups, Australian creatives and international entrants, and the awards were intended to recognise achievements in AI innovation, creativity, consumer work and large-scale business applications. For Victoria's startup scene, Lenexa Medical's result is likely to draw the most attention because of the breadth of its wins, taking category honours in healthcare and the startup competition and then securing the overall Best in Australia award, which placed the company at the centre of this year's judging.

Rostrum AI's award underlined the presence of local business software developers in the field, while SPQR Technologies' win highlighted the attention being paid to AI safety tools as the use of autonomous systems expands. The results come as Australian AI activity continues to spread beyond large technology companies to specialist startups, creative studios and individual artists, and the list of winners suggests judges weighed both commercial application and creative execution across a wide range of work. stories.Headline: Snowflake engineer says enterprises should fix data layers rather than prompts to make AI answers trustworthy
stories.Summary:
Arjun Danda Sureshbabu, a Staff Software Engineer at Snowflake, wrote in SD Times on 2026-11-20 that a few months into building an AI assistant for finance teams, someone asked it what bookings looked like for one region last quarter. The assistant answered in a few minutes with a table and a summary explaining how it got there, and the number was inaccurate. His first instinct was to blame the prompt, into which the team had put role instructions, worked examples and a long description of the schema. When he analyzed the query, the model had done exactly what was asked, finding a table with an AMOUNT column, a REGION_CD column and a date, and summing it up. The model could not know that the amounts included reversals, that region codes had been remapped after a reorg, and that bookings there means something narrower than every row in that table.

The article says most enterprise data was designed for applications and reports, not for a language model reading it cold, and that a finance table is mostly surrogate keys, status codes, amounts and timestamps. It says what those things mean is written down somewhere else, if at all, in a reporting team's SQL, a spreadsheet of code mappings, or the memory of an analyst who has been around for six years. It says a STATUS column with values 1 through 7 will lead the model to decide for itself what they mean, and it won't ask. It says describing the data in the prompt holds up in a demo with five tables and gets shaky at enterprise scale, because definitions and mappings change every quarter and nobody updates the prompt with each mapping change. It says a rule in the ninth paragraph can stop being honoured after a model upgrade, and you find out when a user does.

The article says the teams that get this right stop trying to explain the business to the model in prose and put that knowledge in the data layer, where developers already have tools to build, review and version it. It says that starts with a semantic layer instead of raw tables: named business entities, ontologies, metric definitions, plain-language descriptions of columns and their allowed values, their synonyms and accurate joins. It says bookings gets defined once, in code, and any change to that definition goes through review like everything else, and the model picks from definitions business teams have agreed on rather than creating on its own. It says access control stays in the database, enforced by the same row- and column-level policies that apply to every other query, so the data the model can reach has already been filtered. It says the third piece is making answers checkable, with verified queries reviewed by the owners of those numbers, and when the model writes something new it shows the query, definitions and filters it used.

The article says a prompt tends to belong to whoever wrote it, often one person tweaking it until the demo works, while definitions, policies and verified queries belong to an engineering team with code review, monitoring and someone on call when an answer goes wrong. It says the developers who do this well understand both the data model and the business it describes, sitting with a finance analyst to find out why a code was remapped two years ago and turning that into a definition the system enforces using patterns such as a verified query repository. It says data engineers and domain experts, who often sit at the edge of AI projects, end up doing some of the most important work. It says a better bar than a good demo is whether known or frequently asked questions return the same report the finance team consistently produces, which a human verifies, and whether each answer can be traced back to its definitions and source data. It says prompts still matter, setting the context surrounding the data and how the model asks a follow-up when it is unsure, but they sit on top of everything else.

The article says the author has seen versions of that failure many times since, and the usual response is to tune the prompt, which he thinks is the wrong place to look. It says you can tell the model not to show compensation data to the wrong person, but that is a request, not a permission check. It says moving to a bigger model does not help much, because it writes a more convincing guess and still has no idea when your fiscal year starts. It says you cannot really test a prompt the way you test code. It says most of this is ordinary engineering, schema design, contracts, authorisation and testing, and the unusual part is the consumer, which won't tell you when it's confused or fails silently.

The article says that when an enterprise AI system gives a confident wrong answer, the prompt is usually the last thing the author would change, and he would look first at what the data tells the model, the context layer and grounding factors, and at what it leaves the model to guess. It says the teams keep test sets of real questions with known answers, which is how they tell whether a change actually made things better or just felt like it did. It says the author designs and runs production AI systems that answer questions over enterprise finance data for finance teams and thousands of employees. It says a good answer in a demo tells you very little. It does not say what the finance teams did after the inaccurate answer, or when any of the changes it describes were made.

stories.Headline: CoreWeave and Humatica release a study on scaling proprietary enterprise AI
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave and Humatica released a joint study on November 20, 2026, regarding the scaling of proprietary enterprise artificial intelligence. This research examines how large organisations turn technological ambition into durable competitive value through resilient data architectures and internal governance. The study drew on insights from 252 enterprises across 14 industries and more than 30 interviews with senior executives. The report finds that 66 percent of surveyed organisations operate models or processes that would fail if their systems were switched off. Only 35 percent of enterprises have a formal operating model, while executives cite organisational barriers 2.4 times more than technological limits.

Seventy-three percent move critical workloads to self-controlled infrastructure for proprietary intellectual property, followed by data security at 55 percent and control at 45 percent. Cost and predictability motivate 36 percent of these moves, while 42 percent of production use cases started in business units. Finally, 24 percent of these AI projects were launched independently by employees or small teams. Chen Goldberg, the CoreWeave Executive Vice President of Product and Engineering, stated that businesses are becoming dependent on AI faster than they can run it. She explained that bringing managed PostgreSQL into Kubernetes clusters reduces latency by keeping data calls local and handles replication, patching, and backups.

Goldberg also noted that the connections between compute and data require the same engineering attention as the components themselves. She highlighted that CoreWeave achieved target quality on DeepSeek-V3 2.7 times faster than its GB200 run in MLPerf results. Andy Knobloch, a Partner at Humatica, said that winning leaders are those who decide who owns each AI system and how it improves. He noted that almost half of production AI started in business units without a formal budget or an executive sponsor. The study affects enterprises that rely on AI for core functions but lack the governance to secure and monitor production systems.

These organisations face vulnerability as initial pilots transition into mission-critical applications that require scalable deployment and strict security. The articles state that CoreWeave is the first cloud to publish multi-rack Vera Rubin results in MLPerf and holds Platinum rankings in SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX. CoreWeave also holds first-place inference speed and price-performance rankings from Artificial Analysis for Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.6 and Kimi K2.7 Code. The company partners with CrowdStrike for security, VAST Data for storage, and ClickHouse for real-time analytics. Other partners include Wayve for autonomous driving and PhysicsX for industrial physics AI, while Humatica works with GloCoach for leadership development.

Next, enterprises can use CoreWeave Forge for scalable deployment and the ARIA tool to transform institutional knowledge into proprietary assets. The CoreWeave Zero Trust AI Framework provides security, while Mission Control offers real-time infrastructure visibility across the entire lifecycle. Companies may also use CoreWeave Direct-to-Expert support to pair internal domain knowledge with external engineering expertise. The articles leave open how many more enterprises will establish formal operating models to bridge the gap in organisational readiness.

stories.Headline: Meta AI agents run 1,097 experiments in 31 days to lift search sessions 0.23%
stories.Summary:
Meta researchers deployed AI agents that ran 1,097 machine-learning experiments in 31 days, consuming approximately 360,000 GPU-hours to improve search activity by 0.23%, according to a Nov. 18 research paper. The experiment targeted Meta's search-suggestion system, which determines the recommendations users see when opening the search bar before typing a query. The agents completed 1,097 candidate experiments and accepted 325, representing a 29.6% acceptance rate, compared with a 15.6% acceptance rate in an earlier version of the system. Meta's engineers reviewed a final combined model before testing it on live traffic, where it recorded more search sessions and slower rendering. The live test showed a 0.23% increase in search-session volume with a 95% confidence interval of plus or minus 0.15 percentage points.

The system used Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 to explore architectural improvements and generate candidate changes, letting agents propose model changes, write code, submit training jobs and screen offline results. Meta kept 325 out of 1,097 completed candidate experiments offline, and the live test applied to one combined ranker. The campaign's roughly 360,000 GPU-hours included completed experiments, additional tests measuring training variability, and failed or retried jobs. Individual training and evaluation runs took several hours, making parallel execution necessary to complete the campaign within a month. The paper leaves permanent rollout and a matched comparison with human-only engineering unresolved.

Meta's engineers set the objective, steered the search and reviewed the accumulated model before online testing, while agents conducted multiple experiments simultaneously. The researchers argued that the results showed autonomous agents could perform meaningful machine-learning engineering work on production-scale systems. The researchers acknowledged that the system could not independently identify every trade-off between improving its assigned performance targets and maintaining other aspects of the user experience. The researchers reported that the agents identified several architectural improvements that Meta's engineering team had not previously explored. The researchers did not disclose the size of the slowdown or the financial cost of the campaign.

Other engagement measures, including participation and retention, moved in a positive direction, and the platform handles more than a billion search-ranking requests daily. The new model increased the time the search interface took to render because the agents optimized performance against offline measures of search engagement while researchers monitored interface rendering speed separately. Meta did not compare the resources consumed with those required by a conventional engineering team. The findings leave Meta with a practical question of whether the additional search activity and engineering productivity justify the computing resources and slower interface performance before the model is adopted more broadly. The experiment highlights the computing demands of using AI to improve existing AI systems.

Traditionally, improving such systems requires engineers to identify potential changes, implement them and assess their performance through repeated training and testing. Meta's approach automated much of that process, allowing agents to conduct multiple experiments simultaneously while engineers retained control over research priorities and final deployment decisions. The earlier version of the system evaluated changes sequentially rather than running multiple experiments in parallel. The experiment, detailed in a Nov. 18 research paper, demonstrated how autonomous AI systems can develop and test improvements to large-scale recommendation models with limited human intervention. The resulting model also slowed the rendering of Meta's search interface, exposing a trade-off between automated performance improvements and the resources required to achieve them.

The paper leaves permanent rollout and a matched comparison with human-only engineering unresolved, and Meta did not disclose the financial cost of the campaign. The live test applies to one combined ranker, and the researchers did not disclose the magnitude of the rendering slowdown. Whether the additional search activity and engineering productivity justify the computing resources and slower interface performance remains a practical question before the model is adopted more broadly. The campaign required substantial computing resources, and the researchers said parallel execution was necessary to complete it within a month. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Meta’s AI agents ran over 1,000 experiments in a month but improved search by just 0.23%

stories.Headline: NTT DATA finds Asia Pacific clients more open to outcome-based AI deals than Western markets
stories.Summary:
Nitin Bajaj, the global head of AI strategy and product at NTT DATA, announced at the NTT R&D Forum 2026 in Tokyo that Asia Pacific clients are more open to outcome-based AI deals than those in Europe or North America. This shift is part of a broader strategy called services as software, where AI agents perform tasks that were previously billed by the number of hours or people assigned to the work. The company is moving away from traditional headcount models to focus on measurable results, noting that this appetite for performance-based arrangements has grown over the last two years. The new approach requires different pricing models, including consumption-based fees for high-volume tasks and fees tied to specific results, such as increasing system uptime from 90% to 98.5%. Some contracts involve revenue or profit sharing, such as taking a percentage of profits from a telecommunications call center that exceeds a baseline for new customers.

Bajaj noted that NTT DATA ran over 600 AI pilot projects in 2024, which eventually led to 1,350 paid projects last year. While only about 20% of those specific pilots went into production, the region now accounts for 15 to 20% of pilot volume and is growing quickly. Bajaj explained that the openness in Asia Pacific stems from a diverse mix of frontier, privately developed, and Chinese open-weight models, as well as specific regional capital structures. He admitted that outcome-based contracts are difficult to manage because providers cannot control every variable within a client's business that might affect the final result. He also mentioned that many AI projects fail due to fragmented data in old systems rather than the models themselves, citing estimates that 80% of such projects fail to deliver.

To improve efficiency, the company uses its Silicon Valley firm, AIVista, to reduce document processing costs from a benchmark of 43 cents to about 17 cents. The company is expanding its partnerships with hyperscalers like Amazon Web Services, which has significant influence in the Asia Pacific banking market, and Databricks. NTT DATA is also strengthening its relationship with Google Cloud and expects to have more than 5,000 engineers certified on the Gemini Enterprise platform within a few months. By integrating these tools into a full software stack, the company aims to guarantee the variables that impact client outcomes. This strategy allows them to offer sovereign AI solutions that keep data and control within a specific organization or country.

stories.Headline: Nvidia raises revenue growth expectations as AI demand extends into 2029
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reported strong third quarter results on November 20, 2026, showing massive growth in artificial intelligence demand. The company is currently managing a leadership transition after the departure of its founder, Jensen Huang. Interim CEO Colette Kress is now leading the company during this period of change. The firm reported revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, which represents a 103 percent year over year increase. This financial performance exceeded consensus expectations by nearly 7 billion dollars.

The company raised its Fiscal 2028 revenue growth expectation to 75 percent from 70 percent. Supply commitments rose to 390 billion dollars, including 203 billion for Fiscal 2028 and 92 billion for Fiscal 2029. Rubin Ultra is scheduled for 2027, while the Feynman GPU and Rosa CPU will follow in 2028. Kinsus targets new capacity for 2028, and Siliconware Precision Industries expands packaging into mid 2029. Conditional neocloud commitments of 32 billion dollars extend into 2032 and beyond.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start. She noted that the company roadmap is on track and its ambition has never been greater. Management believes supply will remain a bottleneck through Fiscal 2028 as Rubin begins its ramp. They intend to use 227.3 billion dollars of buyback authorization by Fiscal 2028. The company also plans to return excess free cash flow after making strategic investments.

OpenAI has planned deployments that extend through 2030, showing continued need for compute. Frontier labs, sovereign projects, and agentic AI are also broadening the demand for computing capacity. Some investors worry that AMD or custom hyperscaler chips could take market share from Nvidia. Others fear that China restrictions and higher memory costs could pressure the company margins. Wall Street currently rates the stock as a Moderate Buy with an average target of 232.59 dollars.

Colette Kress has served as the chief financial officer since 2013 during massive revenue growth. Technical leaders like Ian Buck, who created CUDA, remain deeply involved in the company operations. The company has established advantages through its networking capabilities and a large developer ecosystem. Data Center revenue climbed 110 percent to 107.6 billion dollars, with gross margins reaching 74.9 percent. Q3 free cash flow reached 43.8 billion dollars, while shareholder distributions totaled 28.1 billion dollars.

Nvidia expects Q4 revenue of 130 billion dollars, excluding all China Data Center compute revenue. Gross margins are expected to bottom at 71 to 72 percent before recovering in Fiscal 2028. The company will use price increases to help offset the rising costs of memory. Investors are watching to see if leadership continuity can be proven over a longer time. It remains open whether customers will moderate spending if artificial intelligence returns disappoint them.

stories.Headline: Meta AI predicts Cardano will overtake XRP in 2027
stories.Summary:
Meta AI predicted that Cardano could overtake Ripple in the cryptocurrency rankings during 2027. This prediction was reported by journalist Ahmed Barakat on November 20, 2026. The AI suggests that a shift in investor sentiment could enable this change. Network upgrades and renewed institutional interest are also cited as key factors. Both digital assets have spent years competing for attention with different propositions.

The flip requires Cardano to implement the Ouroboros Leios upgrade to increase transaction throughput. The Peras activation is targeted for the second quarter of 2027 to improve settlement speed. ADA could reach a price of 2.50 dollars, creating a 95 billion dollar market capitalization. This assumes a circulating supply of approximately 38 billion ADA tokens. XRP currently has a valuation roughly ten times larger than that of Cardano.

Meta AI is responsible for the prediction and believes Cardano offers a more interesting upside. The AI stated that execution of the development roadmap will be the deciding factor. It suggested that ADA has a genuine opportunity to flip XRP in 2027. The AI noted that XRP remains the more established cryptocurrency in the industry. Successful implementation of upgrades could give investors a reason to reconsider long-term valuation.

Investors seeking outsized returns are affected because XRP needs more capital inflows for percentage gains. Ripple has built relationships across the financial sector to maintain its market leadership. Cardano focuses on research-driven development and decentralized applications to attract genuine demand. XRP competes with an expanding range of payment-focused blockchain networks for its dominance. ADA could benefit disproportionately if capital rotates toward smaller layer-1 networks.

XRP processed an average of 2.48 million daily transactions during the first quarter of 2026. Its real-world asset market capitalization reached 2.25 billion dollars during that same period. Cardano previously reached an all-time high of around 3.10 dollars during the 2021 bull market. XRP has focused on cross-border payments and financial infrastructure for its reputation. Cardano has focused on a carefully structured ecosystem and real-world asset tokenization.

The next step involves watching for higher highs and higher lows on ADA charts. A decisive break above previous cycle resistance could signal a longer-term trend reversal. The articles leave open whether ADA can reach 2.50 dollars without overtaking XRP. It remains uncertain if the Ouroboros Leios and Peras upgrades will be successful. The final outcome depends on whether Cardano delivers on its ambitious development roadmap.

stories.Headline: Danaher and Microsoft build a shared AI platform to speed autonomous lab science
stories.Summary:
Danaher Corporation announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft on November 20, 2026. The two companies will build a shared AI platform for lab instruments. This project aims to advance autonomous science through smart scientific instruments. They want to create an interoperable agentic ecosystem for laboratories. This effort helps scientists move from questions to evidence faster.

The platform uses Microsoft Azure for secure cloud infrastructure and Microsoft Foundry for AI agents. It connects technologies across Danaher while remaining open to other multi-vendor laboratory digital solutions. First commercial applications reach customers this year, including the MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant. This assistant supports Molecular Devices software for high-content cellular imaging systems. Additional agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses are planned for 2027.

Danaher CEO Julie Sawyer Montgomery said the foundation makes instruments work together as one connected company. She stated that context and learning can inform the next experiment and analysis. Microsoft Executive Vice President Deb Cupp said the platform gives scientists more choice and control. Cupp noted that the partnership aligns with the goal of translating AI into real-world impact. Both leaders believe the project makes laboratories intelligent rather than just connected.

The system supports scientists in translating intent into plans and controlling hardware within safety boundaries. It also interprets results in real time and recommends corrective actions for scientist review. Novice scientists using a Leica microscope took up to 83 percent less time in tests. These novices also required up to 68 percent fewer steps than those without the assistant. The AI-assisted users produced high-quality data in time comparable to an expert.

Danaher is a global innovator in diagnostics, biotechnology, and life sciences with 60,000 associates worldwide. The company uses the Danaher Business System to accelerate the delivery of life-changing therapies. This partnership advances a broader strategy for AI and autonomous science by connecting intelligence. It links instrument intelligence with data, laboratory workflows, and the physical execution of experiments. Intelligent instruments serve as the first step toward more connected and autonomous workflows.

The companies are continuing to develop the common agentic platform for instrument control and insight generation. Future goals include using experimental results to help scientists determine what to do next. The platform will allow specialized products to be built on a shared foundation. The articles do not state when the full ecosystem will be completed. They leave open which specific Danaher businesses will launch instruments in 2027.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA becomes official AI consulting partner of the Nitto ATP Finals
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA became a Gold Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, serving as Official AI Consulting Partner and Official Technology Consulting Partner, the company announced on November 12, 2026. The 2026 tournament will take place from November 15 to 22 at Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy. NTT DATA is a global leader in AI, digital business and technology services. The partnership gives NTT DATA a global stage to showcase how AI, data and technology can support human potential. Elite tennis brings together skill, judgment and the ability to adapt under pressure.

NTT DATA will host a Tech Corner in Turin where visitors can see computer vision, Physical AI and advanced AI infrastructure applied to real-world scenarios. Those scenarios include monitoring, safety, construction and humanoid robotics. The space will also house the Mental Economy Gym, powered by Formula Medicine, an Italian company specializing in sports medicine and human performance. Guests there can take on digital challenges that measure indicators such as concentration, reaction and mental workload. At the Fan Village court, NTT DATA will showcase an on-court experience presented by FITP, combining cognitive and physical monitoring with AI-powered computer vision.

Kazuhiko Nakayama, President and CEO of NTT DATA Group, said what makes sport extraordinary is ultimately human, citing the ambition to push boundaries, the courage to take risks and the determination to achieve more. He said technology has the power to unlock even greater possibilities by helping people see what was previously invisible and discover new ways to improve. As an AI Consulting Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals, he said, NTT DATA wants to celebrate human potential while demonstrating how technology can expand what people can achieve. He said NTT DATA combines AI capabilities with deep industry expertise to help clients transform their businesses and create new value. The partnership is the latest in a series of sporting partnerships that bring NTT DATA's global brand positioning statement, "Intelligence to Impact," to life.

IT Brief UK reported that the partnership places the technology group alongside one of men's tennis's best-known season-ending events. The report said NTT DATA will use the tournament to show how AI, data and related systems can generate performance insights and support decision-making under pressure. IT Brief UK said the announcement reflects a wider trend in professional sport, where tournaments, teams and governing bodies use technology partnerships to enhance fan experiences and collect more detailed information on athlete preparation and match play. The report said tennis has become a testing ground for data-led analysis, with systems used across officiating, broadcast coverage and training. IT Brief UK said the demonstrations will place tools used in industrial and operational settings into a consumer-facing environment, linking them to measurable human activity rather than back-office processes.

NTT DATA is a $30+ billion business and technology services leader serving 75% of the Fortune Global 100. It describes itself as one of the world's leading AI and digital infrastructure providers, with capabilities in enterprise-scale AI, cloud, security, connectivity, data centers and application services. As a Global Top Employer, NTT DATA has experts in more than 70 countries. NTT DATA is part of NTT Group, which invests over $3 billion each year in R&D. NTT DATA said it will continue to build on these efforts, using sport as a platform to demonstrate how AI and technology can enhance human potential and create meaningful impact beyond sport.

NTT DATA said the partnership reflects its belief that intelligence comes not only from AI and technology, but also from human expertise and deep industry understanding. It said what matters is how these strengths are brought together to create meaningful impact for clients and society. NTT DATA offers clients access to a robust ecosystem of innovation centers as well as established and start-up partners. The company said its consulting and industry solutions help organizations and society move confidently and sustainably into the digital future. NTT DATA said it is committed to accelerating client success and positively impacting society through responsible innovation.

stories.Headline: Elvis Presley Estate sues Anthropic for $46.6 million over using 274 songs to train Claude
stories.Summary:
On October 23, 2026, the Elvis Presley Estate sued the A.I. company Anthropic, which owns the chatbot Claude, for 46.6 million dollars over copyright infringement. The lead plaintiff is Authentic Brands Group, which owns Elvis Presley's music and likeness, and it claims Anthropic used Presley's songs to teach its A.I. models without permission or compensation. The plaintiffs object to the use of 274 Elvis songs, including classics such as "Return to Sender," "Don't Be Cruel" and "Can't Help Falling in Love." They claim Anthropic deleted information such as composer and publishing details and copied the songs without permission to teach Claude. The suit is one of the first by a recording artist's estate against an A.I. company, and it arrives at a bad time for Anthropic because of its impending IPO, the sale of shares to the public.

The complaint states that Anthropic's guardrails, which were meant to limit infringing outputs, were ineffective and were put in place after the company was caught, which the plaintiffs say shows knowing and willful infringement. The lawsuit contends that from its inception Claude has created infringing output of copyrighted material from virtually every song in every catalog available on the internet. Anthropic has claimed in federal court that its use of copyrighted lyrics to train Claude is legal because it is protected by the fair use doctrine under U.S. copyright law, a common defense in similar cases. A.I. platforms analyze huge amounts of recorded music to learn structure, sounds and expressions, then let users create their own A.I. generated music from what the platform learned. Anthropic developed Claude and released it in March 2023, and the chatbot is also used in A.I. assisted software development and has seen strong sales growth, which could make it easier to defend against a multi-million-dollar lawsuit.

The plaintiffs' attorney, Richard Busch, said the Elvis plaintiffs brought the action to enforce exclusive rights against a defendant that built its entire business model on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before. Musicians have complained that their music and voices are being used without permission, and they fear A.I. generated "slop" could soon replace human-made music. The case is important because it could set a precedent limiting how A.I. companies use music catalogs, and the fear of a bad precedent may push Anthropic to settle. Some A.I. companies have recently begun impersonating artists on music streaming services, and Spotify has indicated it removed songs it considered "A.I. slop" from its user recommendations.
